articles.title: Akshaya Tritiya 2026: How should you allocate gold and silver in your portfolio?
articles.summary: As Akshaya Tritiya approaches, experts recommend a prudent allocation of 15% in bullion, favoring gold. While gold shows long-term potential, silver is suggested as a minor diversifier.
articles.body: A disciplined investment strategy is essential for managing market volatility.  As India celebrates Akshaya Tritiya on April 19, 2026, the bullion market reveals an intriguing yet complex scenario, according to analysts.  Gold, which is presently trading close to ₹ 1,54,650 per 10 grams, has achieved a remarkable return exceeding 63% since last year's celebration—marking its best performance since the rally fueled by the pandemic in 2020.  Experts indicate that gold has reliably rewarded its investors over time, showing average annual returns of over 25% since 2018 and solidifying its status as a dependable store of value.  On the other hand, silver has distinguished itself as the top performer during this cycle. Its prices have skyrocketed from ₹ 95,900 per kg to approximately ₹ 2,54,650—a dramatic 165% increase—driven by robust industrial demand, increasing usage in green energy, and safe-haven buying in light of geopolitical tensions such as the US-Iran conflict.  Nonetheless, experts warn about being overly optimistic in the short term. Both gold and silver could experience a consolidation period lasting 2-3 months as a result of profit-taking and fluctuations across various asset classes. The overarching outlook is still favourable, but investors are encouraged to take a gradual and disciplined approach instead of pursuing prices at high levels. How should you allocate gold and silver in your portfolio this Akshaya Tritiya?  According to Kaynat Chainwala, AVP Commodity Research, Kotak Securities, while near-term volatility in bullion may persist due to liquidity pressures and evolving US Fed expectations, the medium-term outlook remains constructive, supported by geopolitical uncertainty, stagflation risks, and structural shifts in global reserves.  Chainwala advises investors to view any price correction as an opportunity to accumulate rather than exit, while maintaining a prudent gold allocation of 8–15% in portfolios.  For Akshaya Tritiya, Chainwala suggests a slightly differentiated strategy by including silver alongside gold. With its dual role as a precious and industrial metal, silver offers higher growth potential, especially if industrial demand strengthens. A balanced approach is recommended, with gold forming the core 75–80% of the precious metals allocation and silver comprising 20–25%, ideally accumulated gradually with a long-term horizon.  According to Hareesh V, Head of Commodity Research, Geojit Investments Ltd, investors can consider allocating around 15% of their portfolio to bullion, with a heavier tilt toward gold.  Hareesh emphasized that a 10–15% allocation in gold remains a safe strategy given its strong fundamentals, even though short-term movements may be volatile. Silver should be kept below 5%, serving as a minor diversifier.  Further, Apurva Sheth, Head of Market Perspectives and Research, SAMCO Securities added that on Akshaya Tritiya, investors should treat gold as a strategic core holding and silver as a tactical satellite—allocating roughly 70–80% to gold for stability and 20–30% to silver for upside, while staggering purchases to manage volatility rather than investing purely on sentiment.  NS Ramaswamy Head CRM & Commodities of Ventura Securities, believes that with 2026 Akshaya Tritiya around the corner the gold silver allocation needs equal attention. 20% allocation to the bullion pack (10% gold and 10% silver) is recommended in ones portfolio. What is the outlook for next Akshaya Tritiya?  Ajay Kedia, Director at Kedia Advisory, opined that the 12-month targets remain firmly bullish. Gold is expected to test ₹ 2,00,000– ₹ 2,10,000, implying an additional 32-38% upside from current levels. Silver could advance toward ₹ 3,20,000– ₹ 3,30,000, representing a further 34-38% gain.  "We suggest once should Buy — but through Gold ETFs and Silver ETFs via monthly SIP, not lump-sum. Akshaya Tritiya's Sanskrit meaning — "the undying third" — has never felt more appropriate for those invested in bullion," advised Kedia.  Hareesh V said that looking ahead to the next Akshaya Tritiya , gold's long-term potential remains robust, making it a prudent choice for wealth preservation, while silver adds limited but complementary exposure.  Further, NS Ramaswamy believes that by next year's Akshaya Tritiya we expect a rise in gold prices by 25% and silver prices by 35%.  Disclaimer: This story is for educational purposes only. The views and recommendations above are those of individual analysts or broking companies, not Mint. We advise investors to check with certified experts before making any investment decisions.

articles.title: Consumer Durables: 15% डिस्काउंट पर ट्रेड कर रहा सेक्टर, जानिए किन शेयरों पर दांव लगा रहे एक्सपर्ट्स
articles.summary: गर्मी शुरू होने से ठीक पहले बेमौसम बारिश हुई, जिससे समर प्रोडक्ट्स जैसे एसी और कूलर की बिक्री प्रभावित हुई
articles.body: बाजार Consumer Durables: 15% डिस्काउंट पर ट्रेड कर रहा सेक्टर, जानिए किन शेयरों पर दांव लगा रहे एक्सपर्ट्स  Last Updated- April 17, 2026 | 2:49 PM IST  कंज्यूमर ड्यूरेबल्स सेक्टर यानी फ्रिज, एसी, वॉशिंग मशीन जैसे सामान बनाने वाली कंपनियों का कारोबार काफी हद तक अर्थव्यवस्था, ब्याज दरों और लोगों की आय पर निर्भर करता है। भारत जैसे बाजार में कीमत भी बहुत अहम भूमिका निभाती है, क्योंकि यहां ग्राहक खरीदारी करते समय दाम को लेकर काफी संवेदनशील होते हैं।  क्या इस साल मांग कमजोर रही है?  हालांकि इस सेक्टर में नए ग्राहकों की संख्या बढ़ रही है, लेकिन कुछ वजहों से मांग पर असर पड़ा है। गर्मी शुरू होने से ठीक पहले बेमौसम बारिश हुई, जिससे समर प्रोडक्ट्स जैसे एसी और कूलर की बिक्री प्रभावित हुई। इसके अलावा वित्त वर्ष 2025 में जबरदस्त ग्रोथ देखने को मिली थी, जहां एसी की मांग के चलते वॉल्यूम में 25 प्रतिशत तक बढ़ोतरी हुई थी। इस वजह से वित्त वर्ष 2026 में तुलना का आधार ऊंचा हो गया और ग्रोथ धीमी पड़ गई।  यस सिक्योरिटीज के अनुसार मार्च 2026 में समर प्रोडक्ट्स की मांग जनवरी और फरवरी के मुकाबले धीमी हो गई। डीलर्स ने भी सावधानी बरतते हुए पिछले साल के मुकाबले करीब 20 प्रतिशत कम स्टॉक रखा है। कंस्ट्रक्शन सेक्टर से मांग भी थोड़ी कमजोर दिख रही है, क्योंकि लोग कीमतों में कमी की उम्मीद में खरीद टाल रहे हैं। पूछताछ तो हो रही है, लेकिन वह ऑर्डर में नहीं बदल रही, जिससे बिक्री पर असर पड़ा है।  कॉपर महंगा होने से क्या असर पड़ा?  जियोजित इन्वेस्टमेंट्स के सीनियर एनालिस्ट विन्सेंट के ए के अनुसार चौथी तिमाही में कंपनियों की कमाई 8 से 10 प्रतिशत तक ही बढ़ सकती है। मुनाफे पर दबाव बना हुआ है, क्योंकि कॉपर की कीमत साल दर साल 33 प्रतिशत बढ़ गई है। इसके अलावा बीईई के नए नियमों के चलते कंपनियों ने 5 से 10 प्रतिशत तक कीमतें बढ़ाई हैं, जिससे मांग पर असर पड़ा है।  मौसम में बदलाव ने कितना नुकसान किया?  एसबीआई सिक्योरिटीज के सनी अग्रवाल के मुताबिक, कंपनियों ने पहले से ज्यादा स्टॉक जमा कर लिया था क्योंकि उन्हें तेज गर्मी की उम्मीद थी। लेकिन मौसम में बदलाव के कारण एसी जैसे प्रोडक्ट्स की बिक्री प्रभावित हुई। अनुमान है कि एसी सेगमेंट में वित्त वर्ष 2026 में करीब 5 प्रतिशत की गिरावट आई है। साथ ही, कॉपर की कीमत 13,000 डॉलर प्रति टन तक पहुंचने से कंपनियों को कीमत बढ़ानी पड़ी, जिससे ग्राहकों की खरीदारी पर असर पड़ा।  अन्य कारणों का क्या असर रहा?  पश्चिम एशिया में तनाव के कारण गैस की कमी हुई, जिससे कुछ समय के लिए इंडक्शन कुकटॉप की मांग बढ़ गई। इससे किचन एप्लायंसेज सेगमेंट में अस्थायी बदलाव देखने को मिला।  आगे क्या उम्मीद है?  विश्लेषकों का मानना है कि वित्त वर्ष 2027 में इस सेक्टर में सुधार देखने को मिल सकता है और कंपनियों की कमाई दो अंकों में बढ़ सकती है। लंबे समय में यह सेक्टर मजबूत बना हुआ है, क्योंकि लोगों की आय बढ़ रही है, ज्यादा घरों में इन उत्पादों की पहुंच बढ़ रही है और स्मार्ट व ऊर्जा बचाने वाले उत्पादों की मांग बढ़ रही है। अनुमान है कि भारत 2027 तक दुनिया का चौथा सबसे बड़ा कंज्यूमर ड्यूरेबल्स बाजार बन सकता है और 2029 तक यह इंडस्ट्री करीब 3 लाख करोड़ रुपये तक पहुंच सकती है।  निवेश के लिए कौन से शेयर पसंद हैं?  इस समय बीएसई कंज्यूमर ड्यूरेबल्स इंडेक्स अपने औसत से करीब 15 प्रतिशत सस्ता ट्रेड कर रहा है, जो निवेशकों के लिए मौका हो सकता है। विन्सेंट के ए के अनुसार हैवेल्स, वोल्टास, एंबर एंटरप्राइजेज और पीजी इलेक्ट्रोप्लास्ट अच्छे विकल्प हैं। वहीं सनी अग्रवाल ने एलजी इलेक्ट्रॉनिक्स, एंबर एंटरप्राइजेज, वोल्टास, ब्लू स्टार और हैवेल्स को अपनी टॉप पसंद बताया है।  (डिस्क्लेमर: यहां दी गई राय ब्रोकरेज की है। बिज़नेस स्टैंडर्ड इन विचारों से सहमत होना जरूरी नहीं समझता और निवेश से पहले पाठकों को अपनी समझ से फैसला करने की सलाह देता है।)  First Published - April 17, 2026 | 2:49 PM IST  संबंधित पोस्ट

articles.title: Gold prices rise nearly 10 per cent ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, volatility persists
articles.summary: Gold prices have risen nearly 10 per cent in 2026 ahead of Akshaya Tritiya, driven by global uncertainty. Despite volatility and weak jewellery demand in India, long-term outlook remains positive, with investors increasingly shifting towards financial gold options like ETFs
articles.body: Mumbai: As India approaches Akshaya Tritiya — traditionally seen as an auspicious occasion for buying gold — investors are weighing their options as the yellow metal navigates global uncertainty, with prices rising nearly 10 per cent so far in 2026, a report has said.  According to a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd (MOFSL), despite the festive tailwinds, gold's journey this year has remained volatile, marked by sharp swings amid a complex global backdrop and remains constructive in the long-term period.  It highlighted that gold prices are being propelled by multiple global factors, including geopolitical tensions, concerns over slowing economic growth and uncertainty surrounding interest rate movements in the US.  However, these factors have supported gold's safe-haven appeal, intermittent strength in the US dollar and elevated bond yields have exerted pressure, resulting in a non-linear price trajectory, it said.  “Gold is currently navigating a complex global environment. While there are phases of pressure due to interest rate expectations and currency strength, the broader outlook remains supported by uncertainty, inflation concerns and long-term investment demand,” said Navneet Damani, Head of Research – Commodities at MOFSL.  On the demand side, the report highlighted contrasting trends across key markets.  In India, elevated prices have kept jewellery demand subdued and highly price-sensitive, leading to discounted domestic prices. In contrast, China has seen relatively stronger investment-led demand.  The report also pointed out that a gradual shift in India towards financial forms of gold, such as exchange-traded funds (ETFs), indicating evolving investor preferences.  Citing World Gold Council data, it said central banks purchased up to 870 tonnes of gold in 2025, reflecting continued strong buying, albeit at a slower pace than earlier years.  Meanwhile, global ETF demand has shown signs of recovery after earlier outflows, with mixed but constructive trends continuing into 2026.  “We are seeing a gradual change in how investors participate in gold. While physical buying remains important during occasions like Akshaya Tritiya, there is a clear rise in interest towards more flexible and transparent investment options,” said Manav Modi of MOFSL.  From an investment perspective, the report maintained that gold's long-term fundamentals remain intact, supported by its role as a hedge against inflation, currency depreciation and global uncertainty.  Historically, Akshaya Tritiya has also been seen as a favourable entry point for investors, with gold delivering consistent long-term returns despite interim corrections.  On the outlook, the report said gold is likely to trade within a broad range in the near term as markets adjust to evolving global cues. While some consolidation may follow the recent rally, the medium to long-term outlook remains constructive.  Factors such as geopolitical risks, slowing global growth and the possibility of monetary easing later in the year could support prices, while a strong dollar, persistent inflation and weak physical demand may act as near-term headwinds.  For investors, the report maintained a “buy on dips” stance for investors with a medium to long-term horizon.

articles.title: Motilal Oswal Initiates Coverage on Dixon Technologies, Sets Target Price at Rs 14,700.
articles.summary: Investors should consider buying Dixon Technologies with a target price of Rs 14,700.
articles.body: Dixon Technologies Faces Impact of Rising Memory Prices  The smartphone industry has been affected by high memory prices, leading several players to increase prices in order to pass on the higher costs to consumers. As a result, the overall volumes of smartphone markets, particularly in the low and mid-range segments, are likely to decline. This development is consistent with the second scenario outlined in a recent research report by Motilal Oswal , and the company's estimates have been aligned accordingly.  Despite the expected decline in volumes, the research report highlights several positives for Dixon Technologies. The Indian government's decision to relax the PN3 approval process is expected to facilitate the approval of the Dixon-Vivo joint venture. Additionally, the approval of the 74:26 joint venture between Dixon and HKC for display modules, as well as the ECMS approval for Dixon's display modules, are expected to boost the company's prospects.  The next 2-3 quarters are likely to be challenging for Dixon Technologies, with the company facing the impact of lower volumes and margins as the benefits of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme come to an end. However, the company is expected to benefit from backward integration, which will boost its margins in the long run.  Read also: ICICI Prudential AMC: Analyst Sees Target Price of Rs 3800  Recommendation  We reiterate our BUY recommendation for Dixon Technologies, with a target price of INR 14,700. This is based on a price-to-earnings multiple of 55x, applied to the company's estimated earnings per share for March 2028.

articles.title: Small-Cap Index Jumps 13%, Beats Nifty 50 In April: Should You Chase The Rally?
articles.summary: The small-cap segment of the Indian stock market has been witnessing strong momentum, supported by improving sentiment. A decline in crude oil prices from recent highs, easing tensions in West Asia, and sustained retail participation have all contributed to the rally.
articles.body: The Nifty Smallcap 250 has risen over 13% month-to-date as of April 16, outperforming the Nifty 50, which is up around 8% during the same period.  Several stocks have delivered outsized gains, with names like Ola Electric and Gallantt Ispat surging as much as 70% this month. Broad-based participation is evident, with over 230 stocks in the index trading higher in April, including nearly 175 stocks gaining more than 10%.  On April 17, the index advanced over 1% during the session, compared to a modest 0.5% rise in the Nifty 50.  Should You Chase the Momentum?  Optimism around a potential US-Iran deal has improved sentiment, but the sustainability of the rally remains uncertain. The impact of elevated crude oil prices on India's economy and corporate earnings is still not fully clear.  Experts caution against taking geopolitical signals at face value. VK Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments, noted that US President Donald Trump has a history of policy flip-flops, and investors should focus more on actions than statements.  He added that concerns over foreign institutional investors (FIIs) turning sellers at higher levels are weighing on large caps, which may allow broader markets to outperform in the near term due to domestic flows and retail participation.  However, market participants advise against aggressive buying. Arpit Jain, Joint MD at Arihant Capital Markets, said investors can maintain exposure to small- and mid-caps but should adopt a staggered approach rather than chasing rallies.  A strategy of accumulating quality stocks on dips, with a medium- to long-term horizon, remains preferable.  Valuations Becoming Stretched  A key concern flagged by analysts is the sharp run-up in valuations. Uttam Kumar Srimal of Axis Securities noted that small-cap valuations are now near or slightly above historical averages, leaving limited room for error.  This makes the segment vulnerable to sharp corrections if earnings disappoint or execution falters. Additionally, macro risks such as higher crude oil prices could pressure profitability, especially for smaller companies with limited pricing power.  Srimal cautioned that drawdowns of 20–30% are not uncommon in this segment and advised investors to focus on fundamentally strong companies with visible earnings growth and capable management.  Earnings Outlook Remains Supportive  Despite near-term risks, the broader earnings outlook for India remains strong. Tushar Badjate of Badjate Stock & Shares highlighted that India's five-year earnings growth of around 16% is among the strongest in emerging markets.  Consensus estimates point to 12–16% earnings growth for FY27, with potential for 17–19% CAGR through FY28. Historically, such phases of uncertainty have often provided attractive entry points.  Between FY19 and FY24, small-cap PMS strategies delivered average returns of nearly 23%, significantly outperforming large caps.  Strategy: Be Selective, Not Aggressive  Experts agree that while the long-term opportunity in small caps remains intact, this is not a phase for indiscriminate buying.  Investors should focus on sectors with strong earnings visibility such as banking, infrastructure, metals, defence, water management, and healthcare.  The recommended approach is to accumulate gradually during corrections, stay selective, and avoid chasing momentum at elevated valuations.

articles.title: EUR/USD Forecast: UOB Pinpoints Modest Upside Potential with Critical Support Levels in Focus
articles.summary: 4 minutes ago  •  min s read  Singapore, April 2025 – The EUR/USD currency pair exhibits a cautiously optimistic technical
articles.body: posture, according to the latest analysis from United Overseas Bank (UOB). The bank's foreign exchange strategists identify a scenario for modest upside movement, while simultaneously emphasizing the critical importance of several key support levels that must hold to validate this outlook. This analysis arrives during a period of heightened sensitivity in global currency markets, as traders weigh diverging monetary policy trajectories between the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank.  EUR/USD Technical Outlook: Deciphering UOB's Analysis  United Overseas Bank's research team provides a detailed examination of the euro-dollar pair's current technical structure. Their assessment hinges on the interplay between established support zones and emerging bullish signals. The primary conclusion suggests the pair possesses room for a measured advance, contingent upon its ability to maintain footing above specific technical thresholds. This outlook is not a prediction of a major rally but rather an identification of a potential near-term trading range with a positive bias.  Forex markets constantly process information from central bank statements, economic data releases, and geopolitical developments. Consequently, technical analysis from authoritative institutions like UOB serves as a crucial navigational tool for traders. The bank's methodology typically incorporates several key elements:  Trend Analysis: Evaluating the prevailing short, medium, and long-term directional bias.  Support and Resistance Identification: Pinpointing price levels where buying or selling pressure has historically emerged.  Momentum Indicators: Utilizing tools like the Relative Strength Index (RSI) or Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) to gauge the strength of price movements.  In the current context, UOB's emphasis on “key support in focus” indicates that the immediate risk lies to the downside should these levels fail. Therefore, the modest upside potential is conditional, creating a framework where risk management becomes paramount for market participants.  Key Support Levels Under the Microscope  The concept of support in technical analysis refers to a price level where a currency pair historically finds buying interest, preventing it from falling further. A breach below such a level often signals a shift in market sentiment and can trigger accelerated selling. UOB's analysis highlights several of these crucial junctures for the EUR/USD pair.  While the specific levels are dynamic and adjust with market conditions, they generally cluster around recent swing lows and significant moving averages. For instance, the 100-day and 200-day simple moving averages frequently act as major support or resistance zones. Additionally, psychological levels, such as round numbers (e.g., 1.0700, 1.0650), often attract heightened trading activity.  Market participants closely monitor these zones. A successful defense of support typically reinforces buyer confidence and can provide a springboard for the “modest upside” UOB references. Conversely, a decisive break lower would force a reassessment of the technical landscape, potentially targeting the next support tier.  Expert Insight: The Macro Backdrop for Euro-Dollar  The technical analysis from UOB does not exist in a vacuum. It interacts with a complex fundamental backdrop dominated by central bank policy. The European Central Bank's approach to inflation and growth contrasts with the Federal Reserve's, creating the fundamental driver for EUR/USD fluctuations. In recent months, expectations for the timing and pace of interest rate cuts from both institutions have been the primary market mover.  Stronger-than-expected U.S. economic data has, at times, led markets to price in a more patient Fed, supporting the U.S. dollar. Simultaneously, signs of economic resilience in the Eurozone have tempered expectations for aggressive ECB easing, offering underlying support to the euro. This push-and-pull dynamic often manifests in the technical price action that analysts like those at UOB scrutinize. Their identification of “modest upside” may reflect a view that the balance of risks is tilting slightly, allowing for euro strength within a broader range-bound environment.  Implications for Traders and the Broader Market  UOB's analysis carries practical implications for different market participants. For short-term forex traders, it outlines a potential scenario: look for buying opportunities near identified support levels with a profit target aligned with the “modest upside” projection, while strictly managing risk below support. For corporations with international exposure, this outlook aids in hedging decisions and financial planning for euro-denominated revenues or dollar-denominated costs.  Furthermore, the performance of EUR/USD, the world's most traded currency pair, acts as a barometer for global risk sentiment. A stable or gently appreciating euro against the dollar can sometimes indicate a market environment conducive to risk-taking in other asset classes. Therefore, insights from major banks contribute to the overall mosaic of market intelligence used by institutional investors worldwide.  It is crucial to remember that all forecasts involve uncertainty. UOB's analysis provides a framework, not a guarantee. Prudent market practice involves considering multiple analytical perspectives, monitoring real-time price action for confirmation or rejection of the thesis, and adhering to disciplined risk management protocols regardless of the directional bias presented by any single institution.  Conclusion  The EUR/USD forecast from United Overseas Bank presents a nuanced technical picture defined by conditional optimism. The pair's path for modest upside is explicitly linked to its ability to defend key support levels, making these price zones the critical focal point for traders in the coming sessions. This analysis underscores the importance of combining technical structure awareness with an understanding of the underlying fundamental drivers, particularly central bank policy divergence. As always, market participants should treat such forecasts as informed guidance within a comprehensive trading strategy, remaining agile to shifts in both price action and the evolving economic data landscape.  FAQs  Q1: What does “modest upside” mean in UOB's EUR/USD forecast?  In this context, “modest upside” refers to a limited, controlled potential for the euro to appreciate against the U.S. dollar. It suggests a bullish outlook within a defined trading range, not a prediction of a major, sustained rally.  Q2: Why are key support levels so important in this analysis?  Key support levels represent price zones where buying interest is expected to emerge. UOB's bullish outlook is conditional on the pair staying above these levels. A break below support would invalidate the modest upside scenario and likely signal a move to lower price targets.  Q3: What fundamental factors are currently affecting the EUR/USD exchange rate?  The primary drivers are the differing monetary policy outlooks of the Federal Reserve and the European Central Bank. Market expectations for the timing, pace, and magnitude of interest rate cuts from each bank directly influence the relative strength of the dollar and euro.  Q4: How should a trader use this type of bank analysis?  Traders should use institutional analysis like UOB's as one input among many. It provides a credible scenario and highlights critical price levels to watch. However, it should be combined with personal analysis, real-time price action confirmation, and strict risk management.  Q5: Does this analysis suggest it's a good time to buy EUR/USD?  The analysis suggests a potential buying opportunity exists *if* the price approaches and holds the identified key support levels. It does not recommend buying at any price; instead, it outlines a specific conditional scenario where risk and reward may be favorably aligned.

articles.title: Edelweiss' roads trust Citius raises INR 5bn ahead of IPO
articles.summary: Indian transportation infrastructure trust, Citius Transnet, has raised INR 4.97bn (USD 53.5m) from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering, according to an exchange filing
articles.body: The diversified group comprises pensions and provident funds – SBI Pension, HDFC Pension, Larsen & Toubro Provident Fund, ICICI Prudential Pension and DSP Pension – as well as insurers. This includes Bharti AXA, Bajaj Life, Axis Max Life and IndusInd General.  Mutual funds investing in equity, hybrid and multi-asset schemes – DSP, WhiteOak, Axis Mutual Fund and Quant – were also part of the book.  Citius, sponsored by Epic TransNet Infrastructure, is owned by funds managed by Mumbai-based EAAA India Alternatives, an arm of financial services group Edelweiss.  The IPO opened today (17 April) and will close on 21 April, with gross proceeds estimated to be INR 11bn. The minimum lot size is 150 equity shares and multiples of 150 shares thereafter.  Axis Capital, Ambit Private Limited and ICICI Securities are the book running lead managers , and Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas is the legal counsel to Citius TransNet InvIT.  Citius will initially hold 10 highway assets, spread across geographically diverse clusters in nine states. It also has a right of first refusal on 11 more concessions – some of which have been acquired by its parent company – with the remaining awaiting final regulatory approvals, according to a source familiar. Once transferred to Citius, the portfolio will expand to 21 assets totalling about 5,773 lane‑km across 12 states.  EAAA India Alternatives manages more than USD 7bn, spread across performing and special situations credit, infrastructure, commercial real estate, energy transition, and investment trusts.  Infralogic reported last year that road infrastructure trusts with a combined enterprise value of more than USD 12bn were preparing for public listings in an attempt to expand capital-raising options amid increased interest from domestic investors.  The first infrastructure trust to be established in India was for highway assets by IRB Infrastructure Developers in 2017. The list of transportation-focused investment vehicles has expanded to more than a dozen, accounting for more than half the infrastructure trusts registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India.  Foreign investors including Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC, Cube Highways and Infrastructure, CPP Investments, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, KKR, International Finance Corporation and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank have all invested in Indian roads trusts.

articles.body: Key Takeaways  Gold prices up by nearly 10%25 in 2026 amid global uncertainties.  Demand trends are mixed, with India experiencing subdued jewellery demand.  China shows stronger investment-led demand for gold.  Long-term outlook for gold remains positive  Investors are advised to consider buying on dips  Mumbai, April 17 (NationPress) As the auspicious festival of Akshaya Tritiya draws near in India, investors are evaluating their options with gold prices having surged by nearly in 2026 amidst global instability, according to a report issued on Friday.  A report from Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd (MOFSL) indicates that despite the festive influences, gold's price trajectory this year has been marked by volatility, characterized by significant fluctuations against a complicated global backdrop, but the long-term outlook remains positive  The report emphasizes that gold prices are influenced by various global factors, such as geopolitical tensions, apprehensions about slowing economic growth, and uncertainty regarding interest rate changes in the United States.  However, these factors have enhanced gold's appeal as a safe-haven asset, while intermittent strength in the US dollar and elevated bond yields have placed pressure on prices, leading to a non-linear price trajectory.  “Gold is currently maneuvering through a complicated global landscape. Although there are phases of pressure due to interest rate expectations and currency strength, the overall outlook remains bolstered by uncertainty, inflation worries, and long-term investment demand,” stated Navneet Damani, Head of Research – Commodities at MOFSL.  The demand landscape exhibits contrasting trends across major markets.  In India, high prices have dampened jewellery demand, making it highly sensitive to price changes, resulting in discounted local prices. Conversely, China has experienced relatively robust investment-driven demand.  The report also underscores a gradual shift in India towards financial forms of gold, like exchange-traded funds (ETFs), signaling a change in investor preferences.  According to data from the World Gold Council, central banks purchased approximately 870 tonnes of gold in 2025, demonstrating continued strong demand, albeit at a slower pace compared to previous years.  Meanwhile, global ETF demand has begun to recover following earlier outflows, with mixed yet constructive trends continuing into 2026.  “We are witnessing a gradual transformation in how investors engage with gold. While physical purchases remain significant during occasions like Akshaya Tritiya, there is a notable increase in interest towards more flexible and transparent investment options,” remarked Manav Modi of MOFSL.  From an investment viewpoint, the report asserts that gold's long-term fundamentals are intact, supported by its role as a hedge against inflation, currency devaluation, and global volatility.  Historically, Akshaya Tritiya has been regarded as a favorable time for investors, with gold delivering consistent long-term returns despite short-term corrections.  Looking ahead, the report suggests that gold is likely to trade within a broad range in the near future as markets acclimate to changing global signals. While some consolidation may occur following the recent rally, the medium to long-term outlook appears promising  Factors such as geopolitical risks, slowing global economic growth, and potential monetary easing later in the year could lend support to prices, while a strong dollar, ongoing inflation, and weak physical demand may pose near-term challenges.  For investors, the report recommends a “buy on dips” strategy for those with a medium to long-term investment horizon.  Point of View  Marked by geopolitical tensions and economic uncertainties. While recent price increases signal strong investor interest, the report emphasizes the importance of understanding both local and global demand trends for informed investment decisions.  Frequently Asked Questions  Why are gold prices rising?  Gold prices are rising due to geopolitical tensions, concerns about slowing economic growth, and uncertainty regarding interest rate movements in the US.  What does Akshaya Tritiya signify for gold buying?  Akshaya Tritiya is traditionally considered an auspicious occasion for purchasing gold in India, leading to increased demand during this period.  How are demand trends in India vs. China for gold?  In India, high gold prices have subdued jewellery demand, while China is witnessing stronger investment-led demand.  What is the recommendation for gold investors currently?  The report suggests a 'buy on dips' strategy for investors with a medium to long-term horizon.  What role does gold play in investment strategies?  Gold serves as a hedge against inflation, currency depreciation, and global uncertainty, making it a valuable component of investment portfolios.

articles.title: Liquor stocks: Radico, Globus, ABDL, Tilaknagar, USL, UBL rally up to 7%
articles.summary: Listen to This Article  Share price movement of liquor companies
articles.body: Shares of liquor companies Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders and Distillers (ABDL), Tilaknagar Industries, United Spirits (USL), United Breweries (UBL) and Globus Spirits rallied up to 7 per cent on the BSE in Friday's intra-day trade.  Among individual stocks, Globus Spirits soared 7 per cent to ₹1,024.60 on the BSE. Radico Khaitan (₹3,225.05), Allied Blenders and Distilleries (₹574.85) and Tilaknagar Industries (₹472) surged 6 per cent each, while USL (₹1,303.55) and UBL (₹1,515.15) gained 4 per cent each. In comparison, the BSE Sensex was up 0.42 per cent at 78,314 at 01:54 PM. What's driving liquor stocks?  Pernod Ricard reported its Q3 earnings. Its India business outperformed all the other regions. India business organic sales growth stood at 11 per cent year-on-year (YoY) while its 9M revenue growth reported 6 per cent YoY growth.  India business has reported growth vs decline across key market such as the US and China. The company has guided that underlying demand remains strong in India and expects the second half to be stronger ahead.  Pernod Ricard said the India's spirits market continues to enjoy dynamic consumer fundamentals, Q3 benefit from strong underlying demand and continuing premiumisation, along with the disposal of the Imperial Blue business. The broad-based growth across the portfolio with imported spirits in strong double-digits growth, including Jameson, Absolut and Scotch brands, strong growth from local brands, especially Blenders Pride, and with the launch of the new “Xclamat!on” range of Spirits, the company said.  ICICI Securities view on liquor companies  Pernod Ricard largely caters to the whisky segment and has leading whisky brands such as Blenders Pride, 100 Pipers and Royal Stag. Under premium brands the company has Chivas Regal, Jameson, Absolut in its portfolio. The company also notified that its premium brands such as Jameson, Absolut recorded double-digit growth.  Pernod's strong growth in India mainly driven by premiumisation gives a positive outlook for other liquor companies operating in the country. Continued demand for premiumisation in this space is positive for ABDL and Radico Khaitan, who continue to grow their Prestige & Above (P&A) segments. This also provides a positive revenue and earnings outlook for ABDL and Radico Khaitan for the upcoming Q4FY26 and upcoming quarters ahead, ICICI Securities said in a note.  JM Financial Institutional Securities view on Q4 review on Alcoholic Beverages  While demand trends remained resilient in Q4FY26, emerging uncertainty on moderation in discretionary consumption and margin pressures (due to inflation in packaging material such as glass/PET) going into FY27E on account of the ongoing geopolitical crisis have led to a sharp correction across our coverage.  All in all, analysts at JM Financial Institutional Securities said they are cutting FY27E/28E earnings by 1–4 per cent (for ABDL, United Breweries and United Spirits) and lowering the target multiples across coverage, driving down target prices by 6–13 per cent. Accordingly, management commentary on demand trends/pricing actions and margin outlook will be the key variables to monitor to get a handle on future earnings drivers and re-rating potential hereon, the brokerage firm said in the sector update. articles.title: HDB Financial Services set for sustained growth as stress pool declines and margins hold above 8%
articles.summary: The company expects credit cost to remain stable around current levels of 2.3% in the near term, supported by improving portfolio performance across key segments, including commercial vehicles and unsecured lending.
articles.body: HDB Financial Services (HDBFS) is expected to sustain strong growth momentum into FY27, supported by improving asset quality , record disbursements and stable margins above 8%, even as it monitors potential macro risks from the West Asia conflict and broader inflation dynamics.  The company reported a strong Q4FY26 performance, with profit after tax rising 41% year-on-year to Rs 7.5 billion, driven by robust operating execution and improving credit quality, , according to an analyst report by ICICI Securities. Pre-provision operating profit grew 27% year-on-year, while disbursements hit a record Rs 199 billion, up 11% quarter-on-quarter and 13% year-on-year, supporting 11% YoY credit growth for the quarter.  Asset quality improved sharply during the quarter, with the stress pool (Stage 2 + Stage 3) declining to 3.94% from 4.8% sequentially. Credit costs eased to 2.3%, the lowest in six quarters, while write-offs moderated to below 50 basis points. RoA/RoE stood at 2.48% and 14.8%, respectively.  Management indicated that the business has not seen any material adverse impact from the West Asia conflict so far, with rural demand and policy support keeping underlying momentum intact. While external risks such as geopolitical tensions and weather-related factors remain monitorable, no meaningful stress has been observed in asset quality or disbursement trends.  HDBFS expects credit cost to remain stable around current levels of 2.3% in the near term, supported by improving portfolio performance across key segments, including commercial vehicles and unsecured lending.  Growth momentum strong  Growth momentum strengthened through FY26, with disbursements rising sequentially for three consecutive quarters. The company now expects medium-term credit growth of 6–7% above nominal GDP, translating into an estimated 17–18% CAGR over FY26–FY28. The recovery follows a prior slowdown in CV and unsecured personal loan segments, which had temporarily weighed on disbursements.  Segment-wise, consumer finance grew 5.3% quarter-on-quarter, asset finance rose 2.6%, and enterprise lending increased 2.9%, reflecting broad-based growth. Management expects the loan mix to remain largely stable in FY27, with continued focus on all business lines.  Margins improved for the fifth consecutive quarter to 8.23%, aided by a decline in cost of funds and stable borrowing conditions. While yields moderated due to product mix shifts toward secured lending, management expects some upward bias in yields going forward as unsecured lending and used vehicle financing gain traction. The company expects margins to remain above 8% in Q1FY27 as well.  Asset quality trends remain constructive, with improvement across CV and construction equipment portfolios and declining stress formation. Management expects credit costs to remain broadly stable around 2.3%, supported by lower flow-to-defaults and improved collections efficiency.  On growth drivers, HDBFS is focusing on expansion in asset finance, particularly used vehicle financing, where it aims to reach a 50:50 mix between new and used vehicles over the next four years. Consumer finance demand remains supported by durable goods and auto loans, while enterprise lending continues to show improving traction in secured segments.  The lender also maintained that its West Asia exposure remains limited, with no material level 2 or level 3 stress observed. It continues to monitor macro conditions, including inflation and potential weather disruptions, but remains confident of sustaining operational resilience.  ICICI Securities expects HDBFS to maintain its growth trajectory, supported by improving credit quality, stable margins and strong disbursement momentum, while reiterating its positive medium-term outlook on the stock.

articles.title: HDFC AMC starts coverage: BUY call, ₹2,950 target 2026
articles.summary: HDFC Asset Management Company Ltd  HDFCAMC  Coverage initiation and the key call
articles.body: Prabhudas Lilladher has initiated coverage on HDFC Asset Management Company (HDFC AMC) with a 'BUY' rating and a price target of ₹2,950 . The brokerage linked its initiation to a strong quarter for the asset manager, noting that the reported performance was ahead of analyst expectations. The note also lays out assumptions on equity-yield compression over the next few years, which is a central driver for revenue outcomes in AMC businesses. Alongside this, the brokerage has revised its medium-term earnings estimates modestly upward.  The initiation call is one of multiple brokerage notes referenced in the provided material, some of which cite materially different targets for HDFC AMC at different points in time. That range of targets underlines how sensitive valuations can be to assumptions on market levels, flows, product mix and fee yields.  What the quarter signalled for HDFC AMC  The material states that HDFC AMC posted a robust quarter that exceeded expectations. In a separate detailed brokerage excerpt included in the dataset, HDFC AMC's core income was 1.8% above the brokerage's estimate, supported by revenue being 2.7% higher . Revenue yields were indicated at 46.7 bps versus an estimate of 45.5 bps . The same excerpt attributed yield strength to (1) an improvement in equity mix, (2) commission rationalisation and (3) flows into higher-yielding older AUM.  The excerpt also points to changes in AUM mix and market conditions, stating that equity mix improved to 60.3% from 59.9% on a quarter-on-quarter basis due to an equity market bounce back in Q1FY26 . It further notes that strong equity performance in the three-year bucket supported net flows' market share of 15.0% in Q1FY26  Yield assumptions: a key valuation swing factor  Prabhudas Lilladher's initiation note factors in an approximate 2.5-3.0 bps decline in equity yields between FY26 and FY28 . This is described as moderate in the context provided, relative to an 0.8 bps fall expected in FY26  In asset management, even small changes in realised yields can have a meaningful impact on revenue and profitability because fees are typically calculated as a percentage of AUM. The dataset's discussion of yield decline assumptions is therefore relevant for how analysts set long-term earnings expectations and valuation multiples.  EPS revisions and the multiple tweak  The initiation note says Prabhudas Lilladher has raised core EPS estimates for FY27 and FY28 by about 1.7% . Despite the EPS upgrade, the price target remains unchanged at ₹2,950 . The note explains this through a minor valuation adjustment, with the multiple applied to September 2027 core EPS reduced from 37.5x to 37.0x  Separately, another Prabhudas Lilladher excerpt in the dataset mentions an ESOP scheme of 2.5 million shares and a resulting increase in staff cost assumptions for FY26/FY27E by 2%/4% . That same excerpt also described a different valuation stance at that time, including a change in multiple and a target revision. These details reflect that estimates and targets can shift across reports depending on the period referenced.  Industry flow indicators referenced in the note set  The dataset includes a flow snapshot for the broader industry, stating that industry equity flows improved to ₹31,400 crore in Jun'25 from ₹27,200 crore in Mar'25 . It also notes that equity markets delivered strong returns in Q1FY26 , while acknowledging potential volatility.  These data points matter because AMCs benefit from a combination of market-to-market (MTM) gains and net inflows. The same excerpt cites a 10.1% MTM impact in Q1FY26 for HDFC AMC's closing AUM (CLAuM), alongside an uptick in flows.  Broader AMC sector context cited  A separate sector view in the material highlights structural growth potential for the Indian AMC space, citing low mutual fund penetration and increasing household savings. It anticipates 13-15% CAGR for the AMC industry from FY22-26 , supported by digitalisation and a rising investor base.  Within that context, the dataset states that HDFC AMC and UTI AMC were rated 'BUY' in that sector report, with improving market shares and profitability prospects noted as key drivers.  Stock and company snapshot included in the dataset  The dataset provides a company overview stating HDFC AMC is the investment manager to HDFC Mutual Fund, with total AUM of ₹7,50,000 crore as of March 31, 2025 . It also states that HDFC Bank is the promoter shareholder, holding a 52.74% stake as of the same date.  It also includes market data points such as a previous close of ₹5,555.5 , a day high of ₹5,633.5 , day low of ₹5,555 volume of 435,716 , and a 52-week range of ₹3,563.05 to ₹5,927.5 . Market capitalisation in the same snapshot is listed as ₹1,19,679.46 crore , with P/E 45.940 and dividend yield 1.610  Key figures mentioned (from the provided text)  How other brokerage targets in the dataset compare  Alongside the ₹2,950 initiation target, the dataset references other brokerage notes and an analyst estimate range. It states that analysts' future price estimates include a maximum of ₹7,035 and a minimum of ₹4,920 . It also includes entries such as Prabhudas Lilladher's ₹6,175 target (dated 16 Oct 2025 ) and other targets such as ₹6,800 (Motilal Oswal, 15 Oct 2025 ) and ₹6,638 (Deven Choksey, 16 Oct 2025 ) for the same period.  These comparisons are not presented as one consistent consensus in the source material, but rather as multiple notes and snapshots across dates. Readers should therefore treat each target and multiple in the context of its report date and the assumptions used.  Market impact and what investors typically track next  The dataset ties the bullish stance to better-than-expected quarterly performance and controlled assumptions on fee yield moderation. It also signals that staff costs can move with ESOPs and compensation decisions, which directly affects operating leverage in AMC models.  Going forward, the data points highlighted in the material imply that the market will continue tracking equity mix, revenue yields (in bps), industry flows, and any changes in cost assumptions. The next set of brokerage revisions, if any, will likely reflect how these inputs evolve relative to the FY26-FY28 yield assumptions already baked into models.  Conclusion  Prabhudas Lilladher's initiation of coverage on HDFC AMC reiterates a BUY stance and keeps a ₹2,950 target, even after a ~1.7% lift in FY27-FY28 core EPS estimates due to a small multiple reduction. The broader dataset also shows a wide dispersion in targets and valuation approaches across brokerages and dates, underscoring the importance of checking the exact report context and assumptions before relying on any single target. articles.title: HDFC Life Q4 FY26: APE ₹5,250cr, EV up 12%
articles.summary: HDFC Life Insurance Company Ltd  HDFCLIFE  Key takeaway for investors watching ₹740
articles.body: HDFC Life Insurance (HDFCLIFE) heads into the Q4 FY26 results season with the stock trading around ₹740 in early April 2026. The price is well below the 52-week high of ₹972 and above the 52-week low of ₹620, and the stock has delivered a 1-year return of -18% as cited in the note.  ▼ 13.90  Deep Dive Analysis  Against this backdrop, Q4 and FY26 operating metrics matter because they shape expectations on growth, margins, and embedded value. The latest update points to steady premium-equivalent growth but a softer value-of-new-business margin in Q4. Broker views remain broadly constructive, but near-term debate is centered on how quickly margins normalise after the GST transition and product mix shifts.  Q4 FY26 APE: growth driven by group business  In 4QFY26, HDFC Life reported Annualised Premium Equivalent (APE) of ₹5,250 crore, described as in line. This was up 1% year-on-year.  The mix within APE shows different trajectories. Individual APE was flat year-on-year, while group APE rose 10% year-on-year. This split is relevant because product and channel mix can influence value creation and margins, especially when growth is more pronounced in group business.  The update also flags that the company is entering FY27 with a largely completed GST transition, a supportive yield curve, an improving agency channel, and a strengthening protection portfolio.  FY26 APE: ₹16,640 crore, up 8% YoY  For the full year FY26, APE grew 8% year-on-year to about ₹16,640 crore. This places FY26 growth ahead of the near-flat Q4 trend, implying quarterly growth rates were uneven through the year.  The company's stated aspiration is to outpace industry growth in APE. It also expects VNB growth to be better than APE growth, which signals a focus on improving product mix and economics rather than only chasing volumes.  Q4 FY26 VNB: margin slips to 24%  Value of New Business (VNB) declined 8% year-on-year in 4QFY26 to ₹1,260 crore, also described as in line. The VNB margin for the quarter came in at 24%, down from 26.5% in 4QFY25.  The note cites an estimated margin of 24.8% for the quarter, highlighting that the reported 24% was modestly below that reference point. For investors, this matters because VNB margin is a key driver of profitability and embedded value compounding in life insurance.  FY26 VNB: ₹4,030 crore, margin at 24.2%  For FY26, VNB grew 2% year-on-year to ₹4,030 crore. The FY26 VNB margin stood at 24.2%, compared with 25.6% in FY25.  This combination of modest VNB growth and lower full-year margin helps explain why some brokerages are trimming forward margin assumptions. The update explicitly mentions a cut to VNB margin estimates by 150 basis points for FY27 and 100 basis points for FY28, while keeping premium estimates unchanged.  Embedded value: ₹62,140 crore with 15% operating RoEV  HDFC Life's embedded value (EV) at FY26-end was ₹62,140 crore, up 12% year-on-year. Operating RoEV for the year was 15%.  EV and RoEV are closely watched because they bring together expected profitability, growth, and capital strength into a consolidated measure. A 12% EV rise and 15% operating RoEV provide context for how the company is compounding value even as near-term VNB margins fluctuate.  Stock levels and why the Q4 print is closely watched  The stock was cited at a current market price of ₹740 as of early April 2026. The same note highlights the 52-week high of ₹972 and 52-week low of ₹620.  With a -18% 1-year return referenced, Q4 FY26 results are positioned as an important checkpoint for investors assessing whether to hold, add, or reduce exposure. The market will likely focus on the pace of individual business growth, the contribution of group APE, and whether VNB margin stabilises.  What brokerages are saying: ratings and targets  Multiple brokerages listed in the note have positive ratings heading into the results, with targets clustering well above the ₹740 level.  Separately, another excerpt states that Motilal Oswal maintained a Buy rating with a target of ₹930, and a report mentioned Citi also maintained a Buy rating with a target of ₹1,020.  Estimates in focus: PAT and revenue ranges cited  The note also references analyst projections of PAT at ₹450–520 crore and revenue of ₹28,000–31,000 crore, described as continued sequential growth from Q3 FY26 levels.  While these are projections rather than reported numbers, they frame expectations into the Q4 result. Any material deviation, particularly on margins or value metrics, can influence how targets evolve.  Market impact: the margin debate versus growth levers  On the growth side, FY26 APE increased 8% year-on-year to ₹16,640 crore, and EV rose 12% year-on-year to ₹62,140 crore. The company also enters FY27 with a supportive yield curve and improving agency channel, along with a strengthening protection portfolio.  On the margin side, Q4 VNB margin fell to 24% from 26.5% a year ago, and FY26 VNB margin declined to 24.2% from 25.6% in FY25. Reflecting this, one brokerage note kept premium estimates but reduced VNB margin estimates by 150 basis points for FY27 and 100 basis points for FY28, with operating RoEV around 15%.  The same note reiterated a BUY rating with a revised target price of ₹760, based on 2x FY28E EV. That valuation reference indicates the sensitivity of target prices to EV growth and margin assumptions.  Conclusion: FY27 setup depends on margin stabilisation  HDFC Life's FY26 showed APE growth to ₹16,640 crore and EV growth to ₹62,140 crore, while Q4 saw APE at ₹5,250 crore and VNB at ₹1,260 crore with a 24% margin. With the stock near ₹740 and broker targets largely higher, the next key data points are the company's commentary on the post-GST transition environment, agency momentum, and protection mix.  The insurer has said it aims to outpace industry APE growth and expects VNB growth to exceed APE growth. Investors will look for confirmation of that trajectory in FY27 guidance and subsequent quarterly disclosures.  Frequently Asked Questions  See what broke. See what stood.  Related Articles

articles.title: Has Nifty bottomed out? ICICI Securities dissects chart patterns, predicts these 21 stocks could outperform
articles.summary: Veer Sharma  After undergoing 18 months of consolidation and a 16% correction, the benchmark index Nifty appears to have reached maturity in
articles.body: both price and time terms, having navigated multiple headwinds, including geopolitical tensions and evolving tariff policies. This pattern, based on historical trends, suggests the formation of a durable bottom and indicates the potential for the next leg of a bull market, ICICI Securities said in a report. The current market movement closely resembles the volatility seen during the Russia-Ukraine conflict, with a similar magnitude of correction. While the long-term outlook remains constructive, near-term uncertainties arising from global trade dynamics and geopolitical developments have led to a moderation in the FY27 target to 28,800. The trajectory is unlikely to be linear, with intermittent bouts of volatility expected, although strong support is seen around the 21,200 level. In this backdrop, any short-term corrections are viewed as opportunities for investors to accumulate quality stocks and strengthen their medium-term portfolios. The positive outlook is supported by several historical observations. Major corrections in bull markets have typically bottomed out near 17% and found support around the 200-week EMA, often followed by a median rally of about 30% over the next nine to twelve months. Since 1996, instances of four to five consecutive months of market declines have been rare and have generally been followed by a 30% rally over the subsequent six to twelve months. Similarly, phases of exhaustion in India VIX have historically preceded recoveries, delivering returns of around 25% in the following six months. Over the past four decades, major geopolitical escalations have often coincided with market bottoms once uncertainty subsides, with such periods offering strong long-term investment opportunities. Spikes in crude oil prices triggered by geopolitical events have also tended to be temporary, with easing prices often marking a point of market exhaustion and a bottom in equities. In the case of Bank Nifty, post-COVID corrections have typically stabilised in the 20% to 22% range, acting as a base for subsequent gains averaging around 30%. A meaningful recovery in market breadth is also seen as a key signal of a turning point, laying the groundwork for the next phase of growth. Additionally, a decline in the US Dollar index has historically been supportive for emerging markets, driven by expectations of increased foreign institutional inflows. ICICI Securities expects stocks such as Kotak Bank, Axis Bank, Bank of Baroda, Bajaj Finserv, South Indian Bank and SAM India to outperform. In the oil, gas and power space, it prefers Reliance Industries, HPCL, MRPL, NTPC, Tata Power and JSW Energy. Among other sectors, the brokerage highlights Bharti Airtel, Indoco, Elgi Equipment, Data Pattern, Syrma and NRB Bearings as potential outperformers. articles.title: Gujarat Gas Stock Surges 8 Percent on Nomura's Upgrade to Buy Rating
articles.summary: Investors should consider upgrading their position in Gujarat Gas stock due to improving demand visibility.
articles.body: Gujarat Gas Ltd Shares Surge 7.9% After Nomura Upgrades Stock to 'Buy'  Gujarat Gas Ltd shares posted significant gains on Friday, rising nearly 8 percent after brokerage firm Nomura upgraded the stock to 'buy' from 'reduce', citing improving demand visibility in the key industrial segment. The stock was trading at Rs 362.05 in afternoon trade, emerging as the top gainer on the BSE Midcap index.  Nomura's upgrade to the stock was driven by its expectations of a potential demand recovery in Gujarat's Morbi ceramic cluster, where a shift from propane to natural gas is expected to support volumes. The brokerage firm has set a target price of Rs 390 per share on Gujarat Gas stock, implying an upside of around 16 percent from the previous closing levels.  The upgrade to 'buy' was attributed to the government's prioritization of LPG for households, leading to propane shortages that have constrained industrial users. According to a report cited by Nomura, the restoration of disrupted global LPG supply chains could take three to four years, as it remains unclear if it's a temporary production halt or permanent damage. In Morbi, where nearly 78 percent of ceramic manufacturers rely on propane, several players are now in discussions with Gujarat Gas to switch to natural gas.  Read also: ICICI Prudential AMC: Analyst Sees Target Price of Rs 3800  Nomura believes this move could significantly improve the company's growth outlook. The brokerage also noted that Morbi-based producers are planning price hikes of 15-25 percent to offset higher fuel costs, which could aid Gujarat Gas' margins over time. While Nomura has cut its FY27 EBITDA estimate by 8 percent to factor in near-term pressure from elevated spot LNG prices, it has raised FY28 EBITDA estimates by 14 percent on expectations of stronger industrial margins and volume growth.  Despite the sharp rally, Gujarat Gas stock remains down 18.7 percent over the past one year, underperforming the Sensex, which is down 0.3 percent during the same period. articles.title: Has Nifty bottomed out? ICICI Securities dissects chart patterns, predicts these 21 stocks could outperform
articles.summary: The present market motion carefully resembles the volatility seen through the Russia-Ukraine battle, with the same magnitude of correction.
articles.body: Since 1996, situations of 4 to 5 consecutive months of market declines have been uncommon and have typically been adopted by a 30% rally over the next six to 12 months. Similarly, phases of exhaustion in India VIX have traditionally preceded recoveries, delivering returns of round 25% within the following six months.  Over the previous 4 a long time, main geopolitical escalations have usually coincided with market bottoms as soon as uncertainty subsides, with such durations providing sturdy long-term funding alternatives.  Spikes in crude oil costs triggered by geopolitical occasions have additionally tended to be momentary, with easing costs usually marking a degree of market exhaustion and a backside in equities. In the case of Bank Nifty, post-COVID corrections have usually stabilised within the 20% to 22% vary, performing as a base for subsequent positive aspects averaging round 30%.A significant restoration in market breadth can be seen as a key sign of a turning level, laying the groundwork for the following section of development. Additionally, a decline within the US Dollar index has traditionally been supportive for rising markets, pushed by expectations of elevated international institutional inflows. articles.title: Angel One reports 83% YoY growth in net profit; Check Citigroup's new stock target
articles.summary: The shares of the leading stockbroker gained up to 4 percent in today's trading session from an intraday high after the company reported robust performance in Q4FY26 with Rs 3.6 billion AUM.
articles.body: were trading at Rs 301.45 per share, increasing around 3.10 percent as compared to the previous closing price of Rs 292.40 per share.  Q4FY26 Highlights  Angel One Ltd reported a strong quarterly performance, with revenue rising 38% YoY from ₹1,056 crore to ₹1,459 crore and 9.2% QoQ from ₹1,335 crore. Profit also surged 83% YoY from ₹175 crore to ₹320 crore and 19% QoQ, reflecting improved trading activity and operating leverage.  However, the full-year performance remained weak, with revenue declining 2% from ₹5,239 crore to ₹5,137 crore and net profit falling 22% from ₹1,172 crore to ₹915 crore. This contrast suggests pressure on overall profitability despite a strong Q4 recovery, indicating volatility in earnings during the year.  Operating performance also improved significantly, with EBITDA surging 74.6% to ₹598 crore compared with ₹343 crore a year earlier. EBITDA margins expanded to 41% from 32% in the corresponding quarter, supported by operating leverage and improved order activity, the company said in the filing.  The asset management business reported AUM of ₹3.6 billion, while the broking segment's average client funding book remained stable at ₹58.5 billion during the quarter. The company flagged that the first quarter of FY27 may face cost pressures due to higher IPL-related expenses, annual salary increments, provisioning for variable pay, and fresh employee stock grants. On the business front, its wealth management arm saw assets under management (AUM) rise 22.7% quarter-on-quarter to ₹100.8 billion as of March 2026, with the client base crossing 1,900. Additionally, Angel One said its board has approved plans to raise up to ₹1,500 crore through non-convertible debentures (NCDs).  Commenting on performance, Chairman and Managing Director Dinesh Thakkar said India's growing financialisation and digital adoption are driving deeper market participation. He added that the company is strengthening its core business while scaling new verticals, with early traction helping expand its ecosystem and deepen client engagement.  Angel One Ltd received a positive outlook from Citigroup with a Buy rating and ₹340 target price. Q4 saw PAT growth above estimates, while core PBT rose 19% QoQ. Trading orders increased 31% YoY and 13% QoQ, though the MTF book declined 8% QoQ, indicating some near-term caution.  Angel One Ltd is a leading fintech brokerage firm in India, offering digital trading and investment services across equities, derivatives, commodities, and mutual funds. Known for its technology-driven platform, the company focuses on expanding its retail client base, enhancing user experience, and leveraging data analytics to drive growth. articles.title: Angel One Surges 9% as Q4 PAT Jumps 84% YoY
articles.summary: Shares of Angel One Limited surged by 9.6% on 17 April after the stockbroking firm posted a sharp jump in quarterly profit, triggering a strong buying response from the market.
articles.body: In an exchange filing disclosed after market hours on Thursday, Angel One reported a net profit of Rs 320.2 crore for Q4FY26, up 83.5% from Rs 174.5 crore in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue from operations climbed 38.2% year-on-year to Rs 1,459.4 crore, against Rs 1,056 crore in Q4FY25.  Margins improved as well. EBDAT came in at Rs 472.8 crore for the quarter, rising 16.7% sequentially from Rs 405 crore in Q3FY26. The EBDAT margin expanded to 41.7% in Q4FY26, up from 39.4% the previous quarter. The average client funding book held steady at Rs 5,850 crore during the period.  Chairman and MD Dinesh Thakkar said the company is ‘well-positioned to participate at scale in the next phase of growth in India's financial services market.' Group CEO Ambarish Kenghe revealed that roughly 25% of total committed code is now AI-generated, cutting development timelines across the platform.  At 1:17 pm, shares of the Mumbai-based broking firm were up 8.93% at Rs 318.75 on NSE, after touching an intraday high of Rs 320.63.  Feeling overwhelmed by the markets?
