articles.title: Stock markets close lower on profit-taking
articles.summary: Stock markets closed lower in a volatile session on Thursday with the benchmark Sensex declining by 122 points and Nifty closing below 24,200, dragged by profit-taking in banking and financial shares after a recent sharp rally.
articles.body: Erasing its early gains, the 30-share BSE Sensex declined 122.56 points or 0.16 per cent to settle at 77,988.68. The index opened higher and hit a high of 78,730.32 in late-morning trading. However, profit-taking emerged at higher levels, dragging the index down to a low of 77,674.93. The index gyrated 1,055.39 points during the session. The 50-share NSE Nifty dropped 34.55 points or 0.14 per cent to end at 24,196.75. The index moved between a high of 24,400.95 and a low of 24,102.80 during the session. The two key indices had surged by more than 1 per cent on Wednesday following easing geopolitical tensions.  Among the 30-Sensex firms, HDFC Bank fell the most by 1.75 per cent. Titan, Mahindra & Mahindra, Bharti Airtel, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Bajaj Finance were the major laggards.  Trent, Eternal, Adani Ports, Bharat Electronics and Infosys were among the major winners. “Indian markets witnessed a volatile session today, reflecting a shift from directional momentum to consolidation after the recent sharp recovery. The index opened on a positive note, supported by improving global cues and easing geopolitical concerns, but failed to sustain higher levels as profit booking emerged through the day,” Hariprasad K, Research Analyst and Founder, Livelong Wealth, said.  From a macro perspective, sentiment remains sensitive to developments in the Middle East, he said.  “Initial optimism around a potential second round of US-Iran talks helped cool crude prices, offering some relief to inflation concerns. However, the market's inability to hold gains suggests that investors remain cautious and are not yet willing to chase the rally aggressively,” Hariprasad added.  Broader markets closed higher with the BSE MidCap Select index climbing 0.86 per cent and the SmallCap Select index gaining 0.60 per cent. Sectorally, the trend remained mixed, with metals, IT, and energy stocks supporting the index, while banking and auto stocks faced some pressure.  “The domestic market opened positively but closed with a marginal loss on the weekly expiry day after a volatile session, as investors booked profits following recent gains. Markets remain watchful for clarity on the second round of US-Iran negotiations, which will guide the near-term trend,” Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Limited, said.  The session was largely influenced by evolving geopolitical developments, with optimism around potential progress in US-Iran peace talks, which helped stabilise crude oil prices, Ajit Mishra, SVP, Research, Religare Broking Ltd, said.  In Asian markets, South Korea's benchmark Kospi, Japan's Nikkei 225 index, Shanghai's SSE Composite index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index ended significantly higher.  Markets in Europe were trading in positive territory. US markets ended mostly higher on Wednesday.  Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, traded 1.51 per cent higher at $96.36 per barrel.  Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth Rs 666.15 crore on Wednesday, according to exchange data.  On Wednesday, the Sensex jumped 1,263.67 points or 1.64 per cent to settle at 78,111.24. The Nifty climbed 388.65 points or 1.63 per cent to end at 24,231.30.

articles.title: ATP Barcelone | Arthur Fils face au révélateur Lorenzo Musetti, si ce n'est l'inverse
articles.summary: Impressionnant face à Brandon Nakashima, Arthur Fils a un véritable choc à disputer ce vendredi en quart du tournoi ATP de Barcelone. Face à Lorenzo Musetti, le Français va avoir affaire à ce qui se fait de mieux sur l'ocre, même si l'Italien aussi reprend ses marques après des blessures. Entre la puissance de Fils et les arabesques de Musetti, le duel est alléchant et sera riche en enseignements.
articles.body: Le retour sur terre se passe bien pour Arthur Fils. Prudent après sa longue blessure, le Français avait décidé de ne pas participer à Monte-Carlo pour mieux préparer sa saison sur sa surface fétiche. C'est donc à Barcelone que le Français a repris sur ocre, là où il avait atteint la demi-finale l'an passé. Sa rentrée face à Terence Atmane a été timide, mais sa démonstration face à Brandon Nakashima a ouvert l'appétit. Face à Lorenzo Musetti, Fils a de beaux repères à prendre, et l'opportunité de marquer un peu les esprits.  Suivez le tournoi de Barcelone en intégralité sur Eurosport !  Difficile en effet de ne pas être séduit parce qu'a proposé le Français jeudi. Extrêmement puissant, il a assommé l'Américain par la lourdeur de ses frappes. Et, s'il a quelques fois forcé (17 fautes directes), notamment au moment de conclure à 5-2 dans le deuxième set, ses vingt coups gagnants ont montré l'ampleur des dégâts, surtout au vu des six unités de Nakashima dans le registre.  Laisser le temps de jeu faire le jeu  Dire que le Français a failli ne pas disputer ce match. Après une performance beaucoup plus timide au premier tour, où Atmane a eu des balles de match pour le sortir, Fils a montré que son jeu pouvait faire très mal, et qu'avec du temps pour se régler, ses sensations étaient intactes. C'est toute l'importance pour lui, au vu de ce qu'il a traversé, de passer les premiers tours et de pouvoir se régler. Alors qu'on arrive bientôt à l'anniversaire de sa fin de saison dernière à Roland-Garros, accumuler du temps de jeu est capital.  Un fossé à 7685 points : pourquoi la place de n°1 ne peut se jouer qu'entre Alcaraz et Sinner   Dans cette optique, jouer Lorenzo Musetti est un vrai cadeau. Déjà parce que cela permettra à Fils de continuer à emmagasiner des informations, mais surtout parce que le 9e mondial, demi-finaliste l'an passé à Roland-Garros, Musetti est une référence sur terre. L'année dernière, il avait d'ailleurs atteint la finale catalane, écarté par Carlos Alcaraz, déjà vainqueur d'Arthur Fils au tour précédent. Autant dire que l'opposition sera forcément un cran au-dessus de ce que le Français a affronté contre Nakashima. Mais, au vu de son niveau de jeu, il a un coup à jouer. Et les enseignements seront nombreux.  Des cartes à jouer, des leçons à prendre  Déjà, on est curieux de voir ce qu'il va se passer dans la diagonale revers. Le Français a écrasé Nakashima dans cet aspect, prenant le dessus en puissance et concluant parfois en longueur, parfois en court croisé, et parfois même en amortie. Musetti, artiste du revers à une main, ne lui donnera pas les mêmes balles sur lesquelles s'appuyer, mais il n'a pas non plus la même solidité à l'échange. Jeudi, le Transalpin a en tout cas joué une sacrée partie de virtuose face à Corentin Moutet, pourtant habitué aux tours de passe-passe. ” C'était un match très intéressant, très amusant pour moi et je pense pour les spectateurs. (...) Je pense que j'ai joué un bon match contre un joueur qui joue très bien, d'une manière qui me plaît"  Avec un joli smash de revers gagnant, Moutet fait courir Musetti   La capacité - ou non - de Fils d'imposer son rythme face à la créativité de l'Italien sera intéressante et lui servira forcément pour la suite de sa saison sur terre. A ce sujet, on a vu des ersatz contre Nakashima, avec quelques montées à la volée, et quelques amorties bien senties. Réaliser cela contre Musetti sera plus dur, mais c'est aussi une étape à franchir pour passer un cap dans le jeu du Français.  Un duel de revenants  D'ailleurs, Musetti est finalement dans une situation similaire à celle de Fils. Diminué par les blessures depuis son cruel forfait en quart de finale de l'Open d'Australie face à Novak Djokovic, l'Italien reprend ses marques. ” Tous les jours, je me sens mieux, plus confiant. Pas seulement techniquement, mais aussi physiquement et mentalement. Je ne sais pas à quel pourcentage je suis, mais je m'améliore chaque jour ”, a expliqué l'Italien aux médias.  ” Le tirage s'est ouvert en l'absence de Carlos (NDLR : Alcaraz) car il était le favori ”, a ajouté Musetti, ” mais je vais me concentrer sur les matches à venir ”. Forcément, en l'absence du chat, les souris ont des idées. Entre deux joueurs qui reprennent leurs marques, il s'agit plus de demain que de Barcelone, mais le vainqueur pourra avoir de l'appétit en Catalogne, où chacun à des points à défendre.  Au-delà du tournoi, ce match pourrait être une référence. Surtout pour Fils, il faut le reconnaître, mais tout de même aussi pour l'Italien. D'ailleurs, c'est le Français qui a remporté leur dernière confrontation à Indian Wells l'an passé, pour un score de 1-1, Musetti ayant gagné leur première rencontre à Monte-Carlo en 2024. Ce vendredi, l'un et l'autre auront finalement tout à gagner, et le spectacle devrait être au rendez-vous.

articles.title: Boris Johnson Announces Cautious Exit from Lockdown as UK Reaches 15 Million Vaccinations
articles.summary: On April 16, 2026, Boris Johnson announced a “prudent” deconfinement strategy for the United Kingdom following the milestone of 15 million coronavirus
articles.body: vaccinations administered across England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. This decision comes as public health data shows declining hospitalizations and infection rates, yet experts warn that premature easing risks triggering new variants or overwhelming regional NHS trusts still recovering from winter surges. The announcement directly impacts local governance, as city councils in Manchester, Birmingham, and Glasgow now face pressure to balance economic reopening with infection control, even as little business associations demand clearer timelines for hospitality and retail sectors to plan staffing and inventory.  The Problem: Vaccination Milestones vs. Variant Vigilance  Reaching 15 million vaccinations marks significant progress in the UK's immunization campaign, primarily driven by the accelerated rollout of booster doses targeting Omicron subvariants like XBB.1.5. However, genomic surveillance from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) indicates that while vaccine effectiveness against severe disease remains high at 87% for those over 65, protection against mild infection wanes significantly after four months. This gap creates a critical challenge: as restrictions lift, increased social mixing could fuel breakthrough infections among younger, less-vaccinated demographics, potentially straining outpatient services and school attendance systems already operating at reduced capacity.  Local authorities are caught between competing imperatives. In Liverpool, the city council's public health committee recently voted to maintain indoor mask mandates in public transport and care facilities despite national guidance, citing a 22% rise in long COVID clinic referrals over the past quarter. Meanwhile, in Edinburgh, business improvement districts report that 68% of small retailers fear permanent closure if summer tourism seasons face renewed disruption, highlighting the economic toll of prolonged uncertainty.  “We cannot confuse vaccination coverage with immunity permanence. Prudent deconfinement must be paired with real-time variant tracking and accessible booster access—especially in urban centers where density amplifies risk.”  Geo-Local Impact: Municipal Strain and Economic Calibration  The effects of shifting pandemic policy are unevenly distributed across the UK's devolved administrations. In Wales, where the Senedd maintains stricter indoor ventilation standards for schools than England, local education authorities in Cardiff and Swansea have reported 15% lower absenteeism rates since implementing HEPA filtration upgrades in 2025—a measure now being advocated by teaching unions in Birmingham as a cost-effective alternative to rotational learning. Conversely, in Northern Ireland, the Executive's decision to align closely with England's deconfinement timeline has drawn criticism from the Belfast Trades Council, which argues that the region's older demographic profile and higher prevalence of chronic conditions necessitate a more cautious approach.  Economically, the hospitality sector in London's West End shows early signs of recovery, with OpenTable data indicating a 40% increase in restaurant bookings compared to March 2025. Yet, this rebound masks deep fractures: independent pubs in Sheffield and Newcastle report that 30% of their pre-pandemic staff have not returned, citing childcare shortages and wage stagnation. These labor gaps are accelerating demand for specialized workforce solutions, particularly in regions where tourism and retail form the backbone of municipal revenue.  The Directory Bridge: Connecting Crisis to Competent Response  As communities navigate this transitional phase, the necessitate for trusted, locally embedded services becomes acute. Municipalities grappling with fluctuating public health orders require agile public health law attorneys to interpret evolving regulations and advise on liability risks for businesses implementing vaccine or mask policies. Simultaneously, regions experiencing workforce dislocation in service industries benefit from partnering with certified workforce redevelopment programs that retrain displaced hospitality workers for roles in logistics or green energy sectors—initiatives already showing success in Glasgow's Just Transition Zone.  as long COVID cases continue to strain primary care networks, patients increasingly rely on post-viral rehabilitation centers offering multidisciplinary care, including pulmonary therapy and cognitive rehabilitation. These clinics, many of which expanded capacity during 2024–2025, now serve as critical nodes in the UK's pandemic resilience infrastructure, particularly in underserved areas like Blackpool and Middlesbrough where access to specialist care remains limited.  “The true measure of our recovery isn't just in vaccination numbers—it's in how quickly we can redirect resources to those still suffering the long tail of this pandemic. Directory-verified professionals aren't just helpful; they're essential to equitable recovery.”  Macro-Economic Under Currents: Beyond the Headline Number  While the 15 million vaccination figure dominates headlines, deeper economic indicators reveal a more nuanced picture. The Office for National Statistics (ONS) reports that UK GDP growth in Q1 2026 slowed to 0.2%, down from 0.8% in the previous quarter, partly due to persistent labor shortages in healthcare and social care—sectors where vaccination rates, though high, have not eliminated absenteeism linked to long COVID or caregiving responsibilities. This stagnation contrasts sharply with the rebound seen in construction and professional services, underscoring a K-shaped recovery where regional disparities are widening.  the fiscal burden of prolonged pandemic response continues to weigh on local governments. The Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) estimates that English councils faced an average £1.2 million in unplanned pandemic-related expenditures in 2025, ranging from outbreak testing in care homes to temporary housing for isolated individuals. These costs are prompting renewed calls for reform of local government finance, with groups like the Local Government Association advocating for a dedicated pandemic resilience fund to avoid repeated reliance on emergency reserves.  As the UK moves toward endemic management, the lesson is clear: numerical milestones must be paired with hyperlocal responsiveness. The path forward depends not on centralized decrees alone, but on the capacity of communities to access verified expertise—whether legal, medical, or economic—precisely when and where it is needed.

articles.title: Angel One Q4 Results: Profit soars 84% YoY in a quarter of stock market crash
articles.summary: Angel One reported a sharp rise in profit for the March quarter, driven by strong client activity and operating leverage. Profit after tax stood at Rs 320 crore in the fourth quarter, marking an 84% year-on-year (YoY) increase, while rising 19% sequentially. The strong profit growth was supported by higher trading volumes and better monetisation across segments.
articles.body: Total gross revenue came in at Rs 1,467 crore, up 39% YoY and 10% quarter-on-quarter, reflecting improved trading volumes and platform engagement. EBDAT rose to Rs 473 crore, up 17% sequentially, while margins expanded to 41.7%, indicating strong operating leverage.  The quarter saw a rebound in client activity, with total orders rising to 43.1 crore, up 13% sequentially, marking a six-quarter high. The company's client base expanded to 3.74 crore, while its share in India's demat accounts rose to 16.7%.  Despite a slight dip in cash segment activity, derivatives and commodity segments saw strong growth, supporting overall order volumes.  Angel One continued to see traction beyond broking. Wealth management assets under management surged 23% sequentially to Rs 10,080 crore, while asset management AUM stood at Rs 360 crore. However, credit disbursals declined 14.7% sequentially, reflecting some moderation in lending activity.  The company's asset management business remained small but growing, with AUM at Rs 360 crore, while mutual fund SIP registrations remained strong at 2.1 million during the quarter. However, credit disbursals declined 15% sequentially to Rs 610 crore, indicating some moderation in lending activity.  Management attributed the strong performance to normalisation in client activity and increased adoption of digital platforms, alongside continued investments in AI-led capabilities to improve customer experience and operational efficiency.Angel One is positioning itself as a full-stack digital financial platform, expanding beyond broking into wealth, asset management, and credit, supported by technology-led innovation.

articles.title: US Dollar Rallies on Technical Momentum Amid US-Iran Diplomatic Developments.
articles.summary: US Dollar Climbs as Investors Await Iran News  The US dollar experienced a technical recovery on Thursday, retracing some of its recent
articles.body: losses, as investors awaited news about a possible US-Iran peace deal. President Donald Trump's comments that the US-Israeli war with Iran was "close to over" contributed to the dollar's climb against major currencies. The White House expressed optimism about a deal, stating that more in-person talks would likely take place in Pakistan over the weekend.  However, an Iranian official stated that significant gaps remain, including over Tehran's nuclear ambitions, despite the two sides having made some progress. The dollar's recovery is seen as a relief bounce, with the cyclical backdrop for the currency remaining neutral over the next few months. Market participants warned that "peak uncertainty" is not behind us just yet, given the fragile US-Iran ceasefire and questions about the inflation outlook.  Euro Falls from Seven-Week High  Read also: Stocks to Watch Today: HDFC Life, Wipro, Angel One, Waaree Renewable, Om Power Transmission, Rail Vikas Nigam, VST Industries in Focus on April 17.  In afternoon trading, the euro fell from a seven-week high against the dollar of $1.1823, and was last down 0.1% at $1.1782. The dollar index, which measures the currency's strength against six major peers, rose 0.2% to 98.19. The index, whose biggest component is the euro, earlier fell to its lowest level since late February.  Currency  7-Week High  Current Price  Euro  Dollar Index  The dollar index has declined for eight straight sessions through Wednesday to give up most of the gains sparked by the war, as a ceasefire revived appetite for riskier currencies. The index has been on track for its largest daily gain in two weeks, however.  Currencies Retreat Against Dollar  Read also: Netflix Earnings Signal Shift in Focus to Core Business Amidst Clearance of M&A Uncertainty  Sterling was last 0.2% lower against the dollar at $1.3534, after hitting its lowest since mid-February. It rose from the day's lows, however, after data showed UK growth beat expectations in February. Britain's economy grew 0.5% month-on-month in February, the biggest increase since January 2024 and well above economists' expectations for 0.2% growth.  In Asia, the offshore yuan traded at 6.8231 yuan per dollar, down 1%. It rose earlier in the session after data showed China's economy grew 5% in the first quarter, beating analysts' expectations, picking up speed on strong exports and policy support. The Australian dollar, which is often seen as a proxy for sentiment about the global economy, earlier rose to a four-year high of US$0.7197 before falling. It was last down 0.2% at US$0.7159.

articles.title: Netflix Earnings Signal Shift in Focus to Core Business Amidst Clearance of M&A Uncertainty
articles.summary: Investors should focus on Netflix's core business drivers, such as pricing, margins, and revenue, now that M&A uncertainty has cleared.
articles.body: Netflix Stock Rebounds as Company Focuses on Fundamentals  Netflix Inc.'s stock has gained about 28% since late February, when the company abandoned its pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. The streaming giant's shares have risen 0.3% in midday trading Thursday, on track for a seventh-straight positive session.  The company's decision to end the bidding war for Warner Bros. has been welcomed by investors, who can now focus on the key drivers of pricing, margins, and revenue. Netflix's shares have traded at the highest level since December but remain roughly 20% below the record set last June.  In comparison, Paramount Skydance Corp. is up about 5% since it won the Warner Bros. battle, while Warner Bros. Discovery Inc. is down 5%. The disparity in performance highlights the challenges faced by companies in the competitive streaming market.  Read also: Stocks to Watch Today: HDFC Life, Wipro, Angel One, Waaree Renewable, Om Power Transmission, Rail Vikas Nigam, VST Industries in Focus on April 17.  Netflix's strong fundamentals and enviable position in the current landscape have contributed to its recent success. The company is unaffected by market risks such as artificial intelligence and the war in Iran, making it a safe haven against spiking gas prices. This is reflected in the opinions of analysts, who have boosted their earnings estimates for the company.  Earnings Expectations  Netflix is expected to report revenue and net income growth of more than 15% in its first-quarter earnings print. This growth is expected to continue over the coming quarters, with a recent price hike providing a tailwind. Goldman Sachs analyst Eric Sheridan has upgraded the stock to buy, citing a strong start to 2026 as management continues to execute well against its core areas of strategic focus.  Read also: US Dollar Rallies on Technical Momentum Amid US-Iran Diplomatic Developments.  Despite the optimism surrounding Netflix, some analysts have expressed caution regarding the company's growth outlook. After posting a 16% increase in revenue last year, the figure is expected to be 13.6% in 2026 and 11.6% in 2027, with continued deceleration in the subsequent two years.  However, analysts see the company's sticky relationship with its customers giving it a base of support that makes it a relative safe harbor in uncertain times like these. Netflix is positioned as an affordable luxury, making it less likely for customers to pull back and saving money.  Overall, Netflix's recent success is a testament to the company's strong fundamentals and its ability to navigate the competitive streaming market. While some analysts have expressed caution regarding the company's growth outlook, the consensus among analysts is that the stock has further upside potential.

articles.title: In search of predictable returns, pvt equity funds step up office asset play in Q1
articles.summary: Institutional investors focused on office properties in India during the first quarter of 2026.
articles.body: Private equity inflows increased significantly, with office assets attracting the majority of the capital. Investors preferred leased and near-stabilized properties for predictable cash flows. Residential investments also saw activity, primarily through debt structures.  Mumbai: Office properties continued to anchor in India's sector in the first quarter of 2026, driving private equity inflows even as overall deployment remained selective.  The concentration of capital in office assets reflects investor preference for stabilised, income-generating properties with predictable cash flows.  Private equity investments in real estate stood at $637 million across nine transactions during the quarter, a 2.1-fold increase from $300 million a year earlier, according to  'I was touched badly': Salman Khan's actress calls out filmmaker for disturbing audition experience. 'We were 6-7 girls'   ET Bureau  Move also hints at improving confidence in pricing and leasing fundamentals  Office assets led activity, accounting for $529 million, or 83% of total investments, across four deals. Three were equity investments, indicating improving confidence in pricing and leasing fundamentals in key markets.  "The opening quarter of 2026 confirms a direction if not yet a velocity," said Shishir Baijal, international partner, CMD, Knight Frank India. "The doubling of PE investment volumes relative to Q1 2025, combined with a decisive tilt toward ready office assets and structured residential credit, suggests that investors are increasingly comfortable with the risk-return profile in select segments."  The broader recovery in 2026 will depend on faster valuation alignment in the development pipeline and a supportive macro environment, he added.  "The dominance of office investments this quarter highlights a clear institutional preference for predictable cash flows and stabilised income-generating assets," said Anand Lakhotia, MD & co-head of real estate fund at Motilal Oswal Alternates. "In a selective deployment environment, leased and near-stabilised office properties offer better visibility on yields and lower execution risk. We are also looking at select greenfield commercial opportunities where strong sponsors, proven micro-markets and leasing potential can create meaningful value over the medium term."  All office deals during the quarter involved leased or near-stabilised assets, underscoring a focus on yield visibility and asset-level security over development exposure.  Residential investments totalled $108 million across five transactions, contributing 17% of overall activity. Most were debt-led, with four deals structured as credit, reflecting a preference for downside protection amid uncertain exit timelines.

articles.title: Comment déterminer sa capacité d'emprunt immobilier facilement en 5 étapes ?
articles.summary: Au printemps, les projets immobiliers refleurissent souvent avec une question très concrète : « Je peux acheter quoi, vraiment ? ». Entre les
articles.body: simulateurs, les conseils contradictoires et la tentation de viser trop haut, on peut vite s'emmêler. La bonne nouvelle, c'est qu'il existe une méthode simple, en 5 étapes, pour estimer sa capacité d'emprunt sans se raconter d'histoires, et surtout sans confondre montant empruntable et budget d'achat  En 2 minutes, poser le cadre : ce que signifie vraiment « capacité d'emprunt »  Capacité d'emprunt vs budget achat : ne pas confondre montant empruntable et prix du bien  La capacité d'emprunt , c'est le capital que la banque peut accepter de vous prêter, en fonction de vos revenus, de vos charges, de la durée et du coût du crédit. Le budget d'achat , lui, correspond au prix du bien que vous pouvez viser au total  Entre les deux, il y a des éléments qui changent tout : votre apport , les frais de notaire , d'éventuels travaux , et parfois des frais annexes (garantie, dossier). C'est pour ça qu'un emprunt possible de 220 000 € ne signifie pas automatiquement « je peux acheter à 220 000 € ».  Les 3 piliers qui font tout : revenus, charges, durée (et le rôle du taux)  Pour estimer correctement, gardez en tête trois piliers : vos revenus (ce qui entre), vos charges (ce qui sort déjà), et la durée du prêt (le nombre d'années pour rembourser). Le taux et l' assurance emprunteur viennent ensuite comme des réglages qui peuvent faire monter ou descendre la mensualité à effort égal.  Dit autrement : votre capacité d'emprunt n'est pas une intuition, c'est une mécanique. Et cette mécanique se résume souvent à une idée-clé : la mensualité maximale acceptable n'est pas seulement une histoire de pourcentage, elle doit aussi respecter votre reste à vivre  Étape 1 — Faire l'inventaire express de ses revenus « bancables »  Salaires, primes, commissions : ce qui est généralement retenu (et comment)  Commencez par lister vos revenus réguliers et justifiables . En général, le salaire net avant impôt (ou net imposable selon les pratiques) est la base. Les primes et variables peuvent être intégrées si elles sont répétitives et visibles sur la durée.  Astuce simple : faites deux colonnes, revenus stables (ceux que vous touchez tous les mois) et revenus variables (primes, commissions). Ensuite, pour rester prudent, n'intégrez les variables que si vous pouvez les montrer sur plusieurs mois, et sans en faire la totalité de votre dossier.  Revenus locatifs, pensions, indépendants : les abattements et précautions classiques  Les revenus locatifs sont souvent pris en compte, mais pas à 100 %. Il peut y avoir un abattement pour anticiper les charges, la vacance locative ou les imprévus. Même logique pour certains revenus non salariés : on regarde la régularité et la capacité à durer.  Pour une pension (retraite, pension alimentaire reçue), le point clé est la pérennité . Une somme perçue depuis longtemps et bien documentée sera plus simple à défendre qu'un revenu récent ou incertain.  La stabilité des revenus : ce qui rassure (ou fait baisser) la capacité  Deux personnes avec le même revenu mensuel peuvent obtenir des capacités d'emprunt très différentes. Pourquoi ? Parce que la banque aime ce qui est prévisible . Une période d'essai, une activité récente, des revenus très fluctuants peuvent pousser à la prudence et réduire la mensualité acceptée.  L'objectif ici n'est pas de vous juger, mais de vous situer : plus vos revenus sont stables, plus votre estimation peut être proche de la réalité bancaire.  Étape 2 — Dénicher ses charges récurrentes qui grignotent la mensualité  Crédits en cours : conso, auto, étudiant, renouvelable… tout compte  La mensualité de votre futur crédit immobilier s'ajoute à ce que vous payez déjà. Il faut donc lister tous les crédits en cours : prêt auto, prêt étudiant, crédit conso, et surtout le crédit renouvelable, souvent petit sur le papier mais pénalisant dans un dossier.  Une règle utile : si une charge existe chaque mois, elle doit être dans votre calcul. Même si vous pensez la solder « bientôt », tant que ce n'est pas fait, elle compte.  Charges fixes et obligations : pensions, loyers, assurances, impôts mensualisés  Ajoutez ensuite les obligations récurrentes : pension alimentaire versée, loyer actuel, assurance, impôts mensualisés. Certaines dépenses ne sont pas des crédits, mais elles réduisent tout autant votre marge de manœuvre.  Selon votre situation, le loyer peut être remplacé par la future mensualité si vous achetez votre résidence principale et quittez votre logement actuel. Mais attention aux périodes de transition : double charge temporaire, préavis, déménagement.  Les « oublis » fréquents qui font dérailler le calcul (et le dossier)  Les oublis classiques sont souvent ceux qu'on banalise : abonnements, frais liés à un enfant (garde, cantine), ou dépenses contraintes (transport, santé). La banque ne va pas tout détailler ligne par ligne comme un coach budgétaire, mais vous , vous avez besoin d'une estimation réaliste pour ne pas finir avec un budget qui craque.  Un bon indicateur : si vous ne pouvez pas maintenir votre train de vie sans tirer sur l'épargne tous les mois, c'est que la mensualité envisagée est trop haute.  Étape 3 — Trouver sa mensualité maximale avec le taux d'endettement  La règle du taux d'endettement : comment passer de revenus à mensualité plafond  On commence par le repère le plus connu : le taux d'endettement . Il sert à transformer vos revenus en une mensualité plafond . Concrètement, vous calculez vos revenus mensuels, puis vous appliquez le pourcentage d'endettement visé, et vous retirez vos mensualités de crédits déjà existants.  Exemple simple : si votre plafond d'endettement vous donne 1 300 € « possibles » mais que vous avez déjà 300 € de crédits, il vous reste 1 000 € pour le projet immobilier, avant d'affiner.  Ajuster avec le « reste à vivre » : l'alerte anti-budget serré  Voilà la partie qui change tout : le taux d'endettement n'est qu'un cadre, pas un confort. Le reste à vivre , c'est l'argent qu'il vous reste une fois les charges payées, pour manger, vous déplacer, vivre, gérer l'imprévu. Il doit être suffisant pour votre foyer.  Si votre mensualité « théorique » vous laisse un reste à vivre trop serré, votre capacité d'emprunt réelle baisse. Et c'est plutôt une bonne nouvelle, parce que ça vous évite d'acheter un appartement en vous privant de tout dès le premier mois.  Le bon sens bancaire : quand la mensualité théorique n'est pas la mensualité réaliste  Entre ce que permet un calcul et ce qu'on assume sereinement, il y a parfois un monde. Une banque regarde aussi votre gestion : découverts fréquents, épargne absente, dépenses instables. Même si tout semble passer sur le papier, le dossier peut être « recadré » par prudence.  Votre objectif : viser une mensualité que vous pouvez tenir même en cas d'imprévu, sans que votre projet se transforme en source de stress permanent.  Étape 4 — Transformer une mensualité en montant empruntable selon la durée  La durée, levier puissant : ce qu'on gagne (et ce qu'on paie) en allongeant  À mensualité identique, une durée plus longue permet d'emprunter davantage. C'est tentant, et parfois utile pour passer un cap. Mais le revers est clair : plus la durée est longue, plus le coût total du crédit augmente  La bonne stratégie consiste souvent à chercher un équilibre : une durée qui rend la mensualité respirable, sans exploser le coût global, et en gardant une marge pour vivre.  Taux, assurance emprunteur, frais : la mensualité « tout compris » à utiliser  Pour convertir une mensualité en capital empruntable, vous devez raisonner en mensualité tout compris . Cela inclut le remboursement du crédit, mais aussi l' assurance emprunteur dans la mensualité.  Gardez aussi en tête que des frais existent en dehors de la mensualité : garantie, frais de dossier. Ils ne sont pas toujours dans la mensualité, mais ils impactent votre plan de financement.  Repère pratique : estimation rapide du capital finançable à partir de la mensualité  Sans entrer dans une formule complexe, retenez ceci : pour une mensualité donnée, le capital empruntable dépend surtout de la durée et du coût total (taux + assurance). Plus l'un ou l'autre monte, plus le capital baisse.  La méthode la plus fiable reste de faire une simulation avec quelques hypothèses (durée courte, moyenne, longue) et d'observer l'écart. En quelques minutes, vous verrez si votre projet tient sur une durée raisonnable ou s'il exige de trop tirer la corde.  Étape 5 — Tester 3 scénarios simples et verrouiller son chiffre  Scénario prudent / standard / ambitieux : comparer sans se tromper  Pour éviter l'auto-sabotage (ou l'euphorie), testez trois versions :  Prudent : mensualité plus basse, durée raisonnable, marge de sécurité élevée.  Standard : mensualité confortable mais réaliste, reste à vivre correct.  Ambitieux : mensualité proche du maximum théorique, marge plus faible.  L'idée n'est pas de choisir « le plus haut », mais celui qui vous laisse encore le goût de la vie : sorties, vacances, imprévus, et un peu d'épargne. Un projet immobilier solide se reconnaît souvent à sa capacité à rester stable quand la vie bouge.  L'effet de l'apport et des frais de notaire : ne pas surestimer son budget achat  C'est ici que beaucoup se font piéger. Votre budget d'achat n'est pas seulement « emprunt + apport ». Il faut aussi intégrer les frais de notaire et, selon le bien, des frais de garantie et des travaux.  Si votre apport sert uniquement à payer les frais, votre capacité d'emprunt ne change pas, mais votre budget d'achat peut être limité. À l'inverse, un apport plus conséquent peut améliorer l'équilibre global du financement, et rendre le dossier plus fluide.  Check final avant de se lancer : cohérence, marge de sécurité, prochaines actions  Avant de vous accrocher à un chiffre, faites un check rapide :  Votre mensualité projetée vous laisse-t-elle un reste à vivre confortable ?  Vos charges sont-elles exhaustives et réalistes ?  Votre durée est-elle acceptable pour vous, pas seulement « possible » ?  Vous gardez une marge pour les imprévus et un minimum d'épargne ?  Si vous cochez ces cases, vous avez une estimation solide, et surtout exploitable pour chercher un bien sans perdre de temps.  Récapitulatif en une page : la formule gagnante et les points de vigilance  Capacité d'emprunt = mensualité maximale (endettement) + reste à vivre, selon revenus, charges et durée  Voici la révélation simple à garder en tête : votre capacité d'emprunt, ce n'est pas un chiffre magique sorti d'un simulateur, c'est l'équilibre entre une mensualité maximale (bornée par le taux d'endettement) et un reste à vivre suffisant , le tout déterminé par vos revenus, vos charges et la durée  Quand on comprend ça, on arrête de courir après le « maximum » et on commence à viser le « soutenable ». Et c'est exactement ce qui rend un projet immobilier viable, sur la durée.  Les erreurs les plus fréquentes à éviter et les indicateurs à surveiller  Les erreurs classiques :  Confondre montant empruntable et prix du bien, en oubliant frais et travaux.  Sous-estimer les charges réelles, surtout les crédits et obligations.  Maxer le taux d'endettement sans regarder le reste à vivre.  Choisir une durée trop longue uniquement pour « faire passer » le montant.  Les indicateurs à surveiller : une mensualité qui reste confortable, une épargne qui ne disparaît pas, et une marge pour absorber un imprévu sans paniquer.  La prochaine étape logique : affiner avec une simulation et un avis pro (banque/courtier)  Une fois votre estimation faite, l'étape logique est d'affiner avec une simulation plus précise (durée, taux, assurance, apport, frais) puis d'échanger avec une banque ou un courtier. Vous gagnerez du temps, et surtout vous saurez si votre dossier est aligné avec votre projet.  Au fond, la vraie question n'est pas seulement « combien je peux emprunter ? », mais « quelle mensualité je peux porter sans me fermer le champ des possibles ? ». Et vous, vous vous voyez plutôt en scénario prudent, standard ou ambitieux ?

articles.title: Former banker’s viral video on ‘toxic’ work culture sparks debate
articles.summary: "What was expected to be a '9-to-5' job often stretched to '9-to-7' with a six-day work week. We don't even have time to have lunch… we are expected to eat in 15 minutes and get back to work,”
articles.body: In the video, posted on March 10, Madaan said he quit his Rs 17-lakh per annum job citing a “toxic” work culture and intense sales pressure. “I left it because of two reasons — culture and mistakes,” he said, adding that what was expected to be a “9-to-5” job often stretched to “9-to-7” with a six-day work week. “We don't even have time to have lunch… we are expected to eat in 15 minutes and get back to work,” he said.  He also pointed to the pressure to meet steep targets. “Sales is the only job, they said… they expected us to bring Rs 10 crore deals every month,” he said, adding that failure to meet targets created a stressful environment.  Madaan raised concerns over selling costly financial products. “You are expected to sell trading apps at Rs 10,000 a year when platforms like Zerodha and Groww are available for free,” he said. “I can't even convince myself on why the apps are good and why I should recommend these to a customer.”  Highlighting ethical concerns, he added, “I wouldn't even recommend that to my father.”  The video has since gained traction online, triggering conversations around work-life balance, sales practices and employee well-being in the banking sector. Many users also commented on how they left their own jobs for similar reasons.

articles.title: Family-controlled groups shaping India's listed stocks
articles.summary: Why “family-controlled” is trending again in 2026  A recurring theme across Reddit threads and market chatter is that India's economy still leans heavily on a small set of family business groups.
articles.body: Posts often frame this concentration through a “Big Six” idea, linking ownership to sector influence and stock-market outcomes. The point being debated is not whether these companies are listed, but how control works when a family remains the ultimate decision-maker. Several users also connect the discussion to index leadership, because many large family groups sit at the heart of India's biggest listed companies. This focus has intensified alongside India's multi-year market expansion and rising market capitalisation for large caps. Some threads read the trend as a sign of stability, others as a governance risk that needs tighter scrutiny. The same conversations also note that family ownership in India is not static, because many groups are changing how they run day-to-day operations. As a result, the debate has shifted from “family vs non-family” to “how families exercise control in public markets.”  The “Big Six” framing and what people mean by it  Multiple posts cite a commonly shared “Big Six” list to illustrate how a handful of conglomerates shape key industries. In the circulating summaries, Reliance Industries, the Adani Group, the Tata Group, and the Bharti Group are repeatedly named with detailed sector footprints. The same shared list also mentions the Jindal Group, although the snippets being reposted often include fewer specifics in the social summary itself. The larger point in these discussions is the scale of influence, not a precise taxonomy of business houses. Commenters use the frame to explain why a few promoter-led groups can move entire sector narratives like ports, telecom, steel, and energy. They also use it to contextualise why corporate actions, governance headlines, or leadership transitions at these groups draw out-sized attention. Importantly, the “Big Six” label is a social-media shortcut, not a regulatory classification. Investors reading these threads should treat it as a way to think about concentration rather than a definitive roster.  What the posts say about Reliance, Adani, Tata and Bharti  Reliance Industries is described in the shared list as a family-controlled group under Mukesh Ambani, with major exposure to petrochemicals, oil and gas, retail, telecom via the Jio platform, and digital services. The same summary claims Reliance is among India's highest market value companies and became the largest wealth creator in India in 2025. The Adani Group is described as controlled by Gautam Adani's family, with core interests spanning ports, airports, power generation and transmission, coal trading, and green energy. Social posts repeat two specific influence metrics: Adani operates India's largest private port, Mundra Port, and is described as controlling about 25% of India's ports and more than 45% of coal imports. For the Tata Group, the posts emphasise diversification across steel, automobiles including Tata Motors and Jaguar Land Rover, IT services via TCS, consumer products, electricity, aviation, and its identity as India's oldest major industrial group. One frequently repeated claim is that Tata controls about one-third of the steel industry. For the Bharti Group, social chatter highlights telecom leadership through Bharti Telecom and Airtel and also references retail, with one widely cited figure saying it serves nearly 60% of Indian telecom users.  A quick snapshot table of the influence claims being shared  The conversation is powered by a small set of repeated data points that users cite to argue that market power is concentrated. Some figures are attributed to individual groups in the shared summaries, while others are presented as combined influence for the top conglomerates as a whole. The table below reflects only what is stated in the social and media snippets provided.  Listed does not mean dispersed: what 222 listed family firms suggests  One widely shared data point from the Barclays Private Clients Hurun India Most Valuable Family Businesses 2025 report is that nearly 70% of India's 300 most valuable family-run businesses are publicly listed. The posts cite the number directly as 222 listed companies out of 300. In the same discussion, Hurun's Anas Rahman Junaid is quoted arguing that this indicates families are willing to be transparent and use that transparency to raise external capital. That framing resonates with retail investors, because it links “going public” to access to capital rather than loss of control. The same report snippet notes the threshold to enter the top 200 has risen 70% to Rs 4,600 crore, with an overall qualifying mark at Rs 1,100 crore. Social posts also repeat that industrial products led the list by count with 48 companies. Another repeated point is that automobiles have the highest average valuation at Rs 52,320 crore. Together, the top 300 are said to employ over 2 million people and contribute Rs 1.8 lakh crore in taxes, or about 15% of India's corporate tax collections.  Professional CEOs, family boards: the ownership-management split  A major shift debated online is not whether families control companies, but how they professionalise management. Junaid is quoted saying the next generation does not mind being whole-time directors while hiring a CEO to run operations. The same quote suggests family members increasingly retain board seats and weigh in on key decisions rather than managing everything directly. Examples referenced in the circulating summary include Inox, Windgreen, RPSG Group and Reliance as cases where professional hands are hired, while the family retains oversight. The posts also mention Adani Realty as entirely family-owned but run by a professional CEO. This matters for listed investors because it changes what “promoter-led” looks like in practice, especially in complex conglomerates. It also reframes succession risk from a single-person question to a governance-structure question. The broader takeaway from the social discussion is that India is showing “healthy signs” of separating ownership from management, even if it is not uniform across the market.  What research says about promoter stakes and concentrated ownership  The Indian School of Business (ISB) Thomas Schmidheiny Centre for Family Enterprise study “Family Businesses: Promoters' Skin in the Game 2001-2017” is frequently cited in these debates. According to the quoted findings, promoters of family firms increased their stake over the last decade of the study period, while SOEs, other business group firms, and standalone non-family firms saw declines in promoter shareholding. The research covered 4,615 firms listed on NSE and BSE between 2001 and 2017, and is described as a first-of-its-kind ownership-category analysis for that period. The same excerpts highlight that ownership patterns in India are fairly concentrated, especially in family firms, SOEs, and MNCs. ISB's Dr Nupur Pavan Bang is quoted as saying the trend reinforces the preeminent role of family-controlled businesses. The study also notes that non-promoter institutional shareholding is lower in family firms than in non-family firms and fell further between 2007 and 2017. Another point shared is that MNC promoters increased stakes in Indian subsidiaries, while SOE promoter stakes fell in line with divestment policies.  Scale effects: why market concentration keeps showing up in investor talk  Beyond ownership, social posts repeatedly link concentration to market outcomes such as profit pools and index leadership. One often-cited line is that the 20 largest companies in India generate 80% of corporate profits nationwide. Another widely shared metric says the combined market capitalisation of Nifty 50 companies rose from about ₹13.5 lakh crore in the mid-2000s to about ₹201.8 lakh crore today, with an estimated CAGR of 14.9%, attributed to Sriram BKR of Geojit Investments. In that context, investors tend to ask whether the biggest families benefit disproportionately as markets deepen, or whether market depth reduces their influence over time. Some posts broaden the lens, citing a McKinsey 2024 estimate that family-run businesses contribute about 75% of GDP, potentially rising to 80-85% by 2047, and that around 85% of India's incorporated companies are family-owned. Others cite research suggesting nine-tenths of India's listed firms are family-controlled, far higher than in Western markets. A separate recurring point is that India has not imposed an inheritance tax since 1985, which is argued to make it easier to maintain control across generations. Put together, these datapoints explain why “family ownership” becomes a market narrative whenever leadership transitions, capex cycles, or governance debates trend.  The counterpoint also trending: old houses disintegrated, some tycoons fell  Not all social commentary treats family capitalism as a single, uninterrupted story of dominance. One strand highlights that some family-controlled corporate groups that once dominated Indian capitalism have disintegrated over time. The examples repeatedly mentioned include the declines associated with Vijay Mallya of Kingfisher Airlines, Subhash Chandra of Zee TV, and Anil Ambani, along with references to families such as the Dhoots (Videocon), Nambiars (BPL), Mafatlals (Mafatlal Industries), and Ruias (Essar), and the company Ranbaxy. In that framing, the modern landscape is described as being led by three categories: state enterprises, “new capitalists,” and foreign companies, together accounting for close to 80% of combined sales across listed and unlisted companies. This view does not deny concentration, but argues the concentration is now in fewer, more tightly centralised conglomerates rather than broad “old business house” dominance. For listed-market participants, the takeaway is that family control is not a guarantee of longevity or execution. It also explains why governance vigilance keeps coming up alongside arguments about long-term alignment. The real debate in the threads is about which families adapt to competition and professionalise fast enough to sustain scale.  What investors typically watch in family-controlled listed companies  The discussions repeatedly converge on a few practical checks, even when posters disagree on the conclusions. First is promoter stake and whether it is rising or falling, because the ISB study is often interpreted as “skin in the game” signalling. Second is the ownership-management balance, particularly whether professional CEOs have clear authority alongside a family board presence. Third is sector concentration risk, because posts cite large influence numbers across ports, cement, steel, telecom users, and coal imports. Fourth is transparency, often linked to the Hurun-Barclays observation that 222 of 300 valuable family businesses are listed and therefore expected to operate under public-market disclosure norms. Finally, succession planning is watched closely, with social posts noting baton-passing across major business houses and a broader shift of power to the next generation. None of these checks replace valuation work, but they explain why ownership structures trend as a topic when markets are strong. They also reflect a maturing retail conversation that is moving beyond brand names to governance mechanics. In 2026, the central question being asked is how family control interacts with scale, disclosure, and professional execution in India's most important listed companies. articles.title: Money matters: Planning ahead for cognitive decline
articles.summary: By Steve Dinnen  Here's a frightening statistic: About 42% of all people over the age of 55 will eventually develop dementia.
articles.body: The National Institutes of Health projects that new cases are expected to double by 2060.  Aside from the tremendous burden this will place on our health care and social order, there is a financial tangle. How exactly do you manage money when your cognitive abilities have slipped beyond your capacity to make prudent decisions? If you're a wealth manager, how do you work with a client in such a state of decline?  Charlie Bottenberg, an attorney at Brick Gentry PC, and Dennis Markway, regional director of wealth management firm Apella Wealth, discussed this at a recent meeting of the Financial Planners Association of Iowa. These planners, along with investment advisers, have fiduciary responsibilities to their clients and are often on the front lines of spotting cognitive declines that might impair their clients' money-management skills.  Wealth advisers sometimes meet with clients once a year, maybe twice. Monitoring clients who are aging into the timespan when cognitive abilities typically decline will probably require more frequent contact. Markway cited an example of a person he saw fall within weeks from perfectly capable to incapable. And of course, virtual management precludes any sort of personal observation.  One wealth adviser at the meeting mentioned that he once had a conversation with a client who brought up a topic, then repeated it, then repeated it a third time in the span of a 15-minute phone call. This was his tip-off that all was not right. He knew relatives of the client, so he contacted them, and soon enough they were able to step in as authorized third parties with a power of attorney.  Generally, a power of attorney is a legal document that appoints a trusted person (the “agent”) to manage your money, property and financial affairs. But there are several versions: Most people will want a durable financial POA, which is unlike a standard POA and remains in effect even if you become incapacitated, ensuring your finances are managed without court intervention.  Bear in mind that the holder of a POA may have different personal goals, objectives and tolerance for risk. So much depends on the variables of the principal's finances, said Markway, whether they have current adequate cash flows from pensions, Social Security and other sources.  Most POA holders are family members. Naturally, this can create a potential conflict because, as Bottenberg noted, they are in two roles, as a fiduciary and a beneficiary. But here is where the Iowa Prudent Investor Act comes into play: It requires trustees to manage assets with the reasonable care, skill and caution of a prudent investor. (Other states have their own versions.)  It falls on the wealth adviser to develop a relationship with the new, substitute client so they can move forward with the account in a manner that honors the originator.  This is not an ideal situation. But given the reality of what so many families are facing now, and will in the future, it's a workable solution until we find a cure for Alzheimer's and similar diseases.
